title: Puka Nacua injury: Rams WR to undergo MRI after suffering knee injury on final snap, per report
description:
The Los Angeles Rams are holding their breath over the status of star wideout Puka Nacua.
The team reportedly does not believe Nacua suffered a torn ACL, but the imaging set to be done on Monday will determine the severity of the injury.
Nacua suffered the injury on the final offensive snap of the game for Los Angeles with 1:44 remaining in the fourth quarter.
Nacua was the key to the Rams' success in the 20-13 victory that helped bring Los Angeles back over .500 on the season.
This isn't the first injury Nacua has sustained this season, previously missing time this season with a hip injury.
text:
The Los Angeles Rams are holding their breath over the status of star wideout Puka Nacua. The All-Pro pass catcher is set to undergo an MRI on his knee after injuring it late in the team's Week 9 win over the Washington Commanders, according to a report from ESPN.

The team reportedly does not believe Nacua suffered a torn ACL, but the imaging set to be done on Monday will determine the severity of the injury.

Nacua suffered the injury on the final offensive snap of the game for Los Angeles with 1:44 remaining in the fourth quarter. He took a third-and-11 handoff from Matthew Stafford for a 5-yard gain. Nacua got up after a hard hit, but the injury will now be further evaluated.

This injury dampens what was otherwise a stellar day for the wideout. He finished with 14 receptions on 19 targets for 150 yards and a touchdown, while adding 20 yards rushing. Nacua was the key to the Rams' success in the 20-13 victory that helped bring Los Angeles back over .500 on the season.

Nacua is slated to miss time, which further dents what is already a banged-up receiver room. The Rams have already placed fellow wideout Davante Adams on injured reserve due to a ruptured hamstring he suffered in Week 6 against the Cardinals. That injury is expected to sideline him for anywhere from six to 10 weeks when he suffered it.

This isn't the first injury Nacua has sustained this season, previously missing time this season with a hip injury. When he's been on the field, however, he's been among the best wideouts in the NFL and has caught a touchdown in four of his last five games played.

If he's going to miss any time with this latest injury, it could embolden the Rams to make a move for a receiver prior to Tuesday's trade deadline.

title: Chiefs' Patrick Mahomes brushes off injury scare during rout of Jets - ESPN
authors: Nate Taylor, Jeff Legwold, Ian Rapoport, Adam Schefter, Nick Suss, Courtney Cronin, ESPN Fantasy, Mel Kiper Jr, Jordan Reid, Judy Battista
description:
-- Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes was able to play through pain in his right arm after absorbing a massive hit during Sunday's 35-12 victory over the Jets.
"If I'm able to play, I'm going to play," Mahomes, a 10-year veteran, said.
Coach Andy Reid said Julie Frymyer, one of the Chiefs' top assistant athletic trainers, spent halftime helping Mahomes get his right arm loose.
Reid adjusted the Chiefs' offensive game plan in the second half to help Mahomes.
Mahomes' longest pass of the second half was on a 38-yard reception by Kelce in which the ball traveled 15 yards downfield.
text:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes was able to play through pain in his right arm after absorbing a massive hit during Sunday's 35-12 victory over the Jets.

Jets edge rusher David Bailey hit Mahomes' right arm while he was attempting a pass late in the second quarter, with edge rusher Will McDonald IV and defensive lineman Darrell Jackson Jr. also hitting the star QB on the play.

The quarterback grimaced in pain as he was on the ground, then got up with his arm dangling by his side before slowly walking off the field.

But Mahomes flexed his elbow on the sideline, threw a couple of warmup passes and then returned to the game without missing an offensive snap.

"If I'm able to play, I'm going to play," Mahomes, a 10-year veteran, said. "That's part of the game. It scares you in moments, when you get some pains in certain areas of your body. Obviously, it didn't feel great, but I was able to kind of get it worked on a little bit, especially at halftime."

Mahomes said will undergo additional testing on the arm Monday.

"It's definitely something that scares you more than anything," he said. "I feel good now. The adrenaline is pumping. I'm sure I'll be sore tomorrow. I didn't even ice [my arm] when I used to pitch [in high school]. That probably wasn't good for me. I've never had any elbow issues. Hopefully we can stay away from those."

Coach Andy Reid said Julie Frymyer, one of the Chiefs' top assistant athletic trainers, spent halftime helping Mahomes get his right arm loose. Frymyer was also instrumental in Mahomes' rehab this offseason after he had surgery in December to repair the torn ACL and LCL in his left knee.

"Any time it's elbows and knees, it's always scary, just because you just don't know," Mahomes said. "Even my knee last year, after we were doing the initial test, I thought, because I could walk off the field, I was going to be good. Then, all of a sudden, you do one test, and you're just out [for the rest of the season]. That stuff scares you. Once I could throw the ball, I knew it wasn't a ligament and it was more muscles."

Reid adjusted the Chiefs' offensive game plan in the second half to help Mahomes. Most of the QB's completions in the third quarter were on short throws, leading to yards after the catch for skill players such as running back Kenneth Walker III and receiver Xavier Worthy.

"I'm just glad he was able to finish the game with us," Walker said of Mahomes. "That's the type of competitor he is, a great leader of the team. He'll continue to be that way."

The Chiefs' opening drive of the third quarter ended with a 1-yard touchdown run, a play in which Mahomes used both hands to push the ball backward to tight end Travis Kelce, who ran with the ball behind fellow tight ends Noah Gray and Jake Briningstool to score on fourth down.

"Pat did some nice things, even with the sore arm," Reid said. "He hurt his elbow region there but was able to come back. He's a tough kid. If there's any way he can come back from something, he's coming back. I didn't know until we were getting ready to start that [next] series."

Mahomes averaged just 2.8 air yards per attempt, his second fewest in a game in his career, according to Next Gen Stats. He finished with 23 completions on 31 attempts for 242 yards and two touchdowns, both occurring before the injury.

Mahomes' longest pass of the second half was on a 38-yard reception by Kelce in which the ball traveled 15 yards downfield.

"Out of halftime, I wasn't throwing the ball the way I wanted to," Mahomes said. "But as the game went on, as we kind of continued to work through it, [my arm] kind of got warmed back up. I thought I started throwing the ball better. That will be important this week, getting that swelling and the fluid out of it, so I can be ready to go from the first snap next week."

text:
NEW ORLEANS -- Browns coach Todd Monken said he was "proud" of Shedeur Sanders after his two-touchdown performance in Cleveland's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints but refused to answer whether Sanders made a case to start at quarterback going forward.

Sanders made his first start of the season as Deshaun Watson was inactive after sitting out two days of practice while sidelined in the NFL's concussion protocol. Watson returned to practice Friday and cleared the protocol Saturday, but Sanders took all the first-team reps in practice. Sanders completed 19 of 31 passes for 297 yards and two touchdowns, leading the Browns on a late field goal drive to send the game to overtime and connected with Harold Fannin Jr. on a 39-yard touchdown pass in overtime but his last-ditch pass on a 2-point try to win the game fell incomplete.

"I'm really proud of him," Monken said. "I mean, I'm really proud of him and how hard he's worked since I've been here. He wasn't perfect. I wasn't perfect. But for a guy that really hasn't taken snaps with the ones in what, 10 weeks, and we announced him with two weeks left, and you're eight weeks into the season, so you're facing 2½ months, you're basically running cards to come in there and continue to battle, really, really proud of him.

"He's really mature. And I don't mean that in a negative way, [that] he was immature. That's unfair. That's not what I mean. What I mean is in terms of his work ethic, in terms of his diligence, in terms of what he will say to the coaching staff and ask the questions, his feedback, those are all the right steps moving forward as any young player, especially a quarterback."

But when asked if Sanders made a case to start again, Monken said: "How long has it been? Thirty minutes since the game ended? I'm not getting into quarterback. If we want to talk about Shedeur, we can talk about Shedeur."

Sanders, a 2025 fifth-round pick, served as the backup for the first eight games of the season after losing a quarterback competition to Watson in training camp. Watson led the Browns to a 5-3 record, in large part because of an NFL-high five winning drives but entered Week 9 with a 40.9 QBR that ranks 28th out of 30 qualifying quarterbacks. Sanders registered a 39 QBR against the Saints, his second-highest mark in a game in his career.

After a slow start, Sanders heated up in the second half with a pair of 60-yard completions to rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston and then a 64-yard touchdown pass to KC Concepcion that gave Cleveland a 13-9 lead late in the fourth quarter. Sanders' two 60-yard throws doubled the amount Watson had in his first eight games.

"I would say I feel the best when a lot of pressure's on," Sanders said. "That's when I feel the best, honestly. And the Saints did a great job of, of course, their getback on tracks, third downs, and how they got to their scheme. But I think in my mind, I think about things like an algorithm, so it's not going to take me long, I would say, to figure what I need out and within the scheme of our offense and what we need to do to move the ball down the field and do what we have to do."

Sanders also clarified pregame comments that he made Wednesday about the Saints' defense in which he smiled when asked what he sees on film and said: "I've seen a lot. When I smile, just know that means something. I'm maturing. I'm maturing. Like, I could have given a decent answer, but now I'm just going to smile whenever it's just, like, some questions."

After Sunday's loss, Sanders said, "My intention when referring to the Saints' defense and how they are, I was never ever throwing a shot, especially [at Carl] Granderson. So I apologize if my words were taken out of context. So I apologize for that being taken out of context, but that's just how media is sometimes. But then also that's on me for not making it very clear. And I understand that.

"I never would talk down on anybody, on any person, because I understand how hard it is just to be in the league. I would say how hard it is to come to work every day and be able to callous your mind, callous your body throughout everything, when things are good, and things go bad. So I just want to make that clear at first. I was never speaking negatively about anybody or any defense."

Granderson, who sacked Sanders twice, said he interpreted the pregame comments differently.

"I don't think we were motivated, though. I mean, we seen him chirping," Granderson said after the game. "So we just came into this game ready to play, won the game on defense. I think it's disrespectful for somebody to laugh at our defense, took us as a joke. So we went out there and balled out. They had 2.8 yards a carry and we stopped the run. ... So we did our thing. Won the game in overtime, 2-point conversion. So that was a good team win on defense."

ESPN's Katherine Terrell contributed to this report.

Rams receiver Puka Nacua tied the franchise record for 10-catch games on Sunday, with a 14-catch, 150-yard performance in a 20-13 win over the Commanders. But it was a rushing attempt that created a major potential problem for Nacua and the Rams.

Via ESPN, Nacua suffered a knee injury on the Rams’ final offensive snap of the game — a handoff to Nacua for a five-yard gain on third and 11.

For now, the Rams (per the report) do not believe Nacua suffered a torn ACL. He’ll have an MRI on Monday to assess the extent of the damage.

As one source with knowledge of the situation tells PFT, “We will see. Waiting on images.”

If Nacua misses any time, it will significantly hamper the Rams’ passing game. Davante Adams remains on injured reserve with a significant hamstring injury. The only other receivers to catch passes on Sunday were Konata Mumpfield (two for 20 yards) and Tutu Atwell (two for 16 yards).

The situation could put the eff-them-picks Rams in overdrive at the deadline, scouring any and all depth charts for help. And, in turn, driving up the price tag for anyone who may be available — from Josh Downs to Brian Thomas Jr. to anyone/everyone for whom the Rams would be willing to make an offer.

Next Sunday, the Rams visit the Cardinals. The Rams have a bye in Week 11.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers' offense will have one more weapon available on Sunday night when they take on the Chicago Bears, as second-year wide receiver Emeka Egbuka, who was listed as questionable due to a foot injury on Friday's injury report, has been cleared to play. Despite missing the past two games due to that ailment and a concussion, Egbuka leads the Buccaneers with 28 catches and two touchdown receptions.

The Buccaneers' defense, however, will be without a key component as outside linebacker Yaya Diaby has been sidelined by a knee injury suffered last Sunday against Atlanta. The Buccaneers will be down to a four-man rotation at edge rusher with Rueben Bain Jr., Al-Quadin Muhammad, David Walker and Anthony Nelson.

The Buccaneers and Bears submitted their list of inactives at 6:52 p.m. ET on Sunday, 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff of their Week Nine meeting at Soldier Field. The Buccaneers did not make any practice squad elevations this week and thus have 53 available players on Sunday, meaning they had to name five inactives to get down to the game-day limit of 48. The Bears elevated running back Salvon Ahmed from the practice squad to a roster that had 52 players and therefore had to name five players inactive.

The Bears will be without one half of their very effective backfield duo, as running back Kyle Monangai will miss a fifth straight game due to thumb and toe injuries. In addition, rookie cornerback Malik Muhammad is out due to a toe injury but fellow cornerback Tyrique Stevenson, who was a late-week addition to the injury report, has been cleared to play.

Tyler Shough found Juwan Johnson for what proved the game-winning touchdown in overtime as the New Orleans Saints stopped a do-or-die, two-point conversion from the Cleveland Browns to clinch a thrilling 23-22 victory.

After the Saints (3-5) scored on the first possession of overtime, Cleveland answered when Harold Fannin Jr turned a short catch from Browns backup QB Shedeur Sanders into a tackle-breaking, 39-yard TD with a minute left in OT.

The Browns (5-4) then elected to try a two-point conversion for the win, but Sanders was forced to roll right under pressure from Carl Granderson and threw incomplete along the sideline, giving the Saints their first home win of the season.

The thrilling finish followed a largely ugly first 54 minutes during which neither team scored a touchdown in which the Saints led 9-6 after three Charlie Smyth field goals

Bo Nix threw for 237 yards and two touchdowns as the Denver Broncos benefitted from a momentum-turning coach's challenge to beat the Carolina Panthers 26-21 for a fifth straight win.

Jonah Coleman ran for 57 yards and a score, while Courtland Sutton and Pat Bryant each caught TD passes for the Broncos (7-2). Young finished 28 of 39 for 276 yards with three touchdown passes and an interception for Carolina (3-5), who have lost three straight.

The Panthers took the lead early in the third quarter when Young found Darren Waller over the middle for a 15-yard touchdown pass. But the turning point came late in the third quarter when Broncos coach Sean Payton won a key challenge.

With Carolina facing a first-and-goal at the Denver goal-line, Young threw a pass towards the corner of the end zone that was initially ruled incomplete. Upon review, officials ruled that Denver safety Devon Key had intercepted the ball that deflected off tight end Tommy Tremble's hand before it hit the ground.

The interception gave the Broncos the ball at their 20-yard line and ended Carolina's momentum and their chance to go up by eight.

Instead, with Denver leading by five, Nik Bonitto came up with a strip-sack on Bryce Young and recovered the ball near midfield with 1:24 left. The Broncos picked up one first down to seal the win.

Los Angeles Rams 20-13 Washington Commanders

Myles Garrett had three sacks and a forced fumble on his return for the Los Angeles Rams as they held on for a third straight victory with a 20-13 road win over the Washington Commanders.

Puka Nacua was targeted a massive 19 times by Matthew Stafford in the contest and finished with 14 catches for 150 yards and a touchdown as the Rams (5-4) moved above .500 for the first time this season.

However, Nacua appeared to injure his knee on the team's final offensive snap and will undergo an MRI on Monday to determine the extent of the injury. According to reports, the team's initial belief is that he did not suffer a torn ACL.

Stafford completed 26 of 43 passing, for 219 yards an an interception along with his seven-yard TD toss to Nacua that broke a 13-13 tie early in the fourth quarter.

Garrett gave a lift to the Rams' defense in his first action since Los Angeles' season-opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia. The All-Pro defensive end then missed their last seven games with a knee injury.

Jayden Daniels went 21 of 28 for 204 yards and a touchdown and had 15 yards rushing for the Commanders (2-5-1), who couldn't generate enough offense to keep up with the Rams.

New York Giants 19-11 Philadelphia Eagles

Jameis Winston replaced the injured JJ McCarthy long enough to throw a go-ahead touchdown pass and help the New York Giants keep their grip on the NFC East by beating the Philadelphia 19-11.

The Eagles (2-7) suffered a seventh straight defeat, their longest losing streak since they lost eight in a row in Andy Reid's final season as head coach in 2012.

The Giants (5-2-1) are the only team in the NFC East with a winning record. The Eagles had beaten the Giants 13 straight times at home - including one playoff win - since New York last won in October 2013.

McCarthy suffered a hip injury in the third quarter that briefly forced him out of the game, with the Giants trailing 8-6, but Winston - who held the starting job for four games after starting QB Jaxson Dart was injured - did enough in his cameo to keep New York's first division title since 2011 within reach.

His five-yard TD pass to tight end Isaiah Likely sent the Giants into the fourth quarter with a 13.-8 lead. McCarthy returned for the final play of the third quarter. He completed 12 of 19 passes for 127 yards and no touchdowns or interceptions. Winston was 6 of 8 for 71 yards and the lone scoring strike.

Patrick Mahomes threw for 242 yards and a pair of touchdown passes to Kenneth Walker, who added 102 yards and a score on the ground, as the Kansas City Chiefs secured a 35-12 rout of the New York Jets.

One week after Jets kicker Jason Sanders made four field goals in a loss to the Las Vegas Raiders, he made four in the first half alone in Kansas City as New York trailed by only two down 14-12 at half-time. It would have been five had Sanders not missed from 53 yards with less than a minute to go before the interval.

Both he and Travis Kelce briefly looked concerned about his prospects of playing, only for the three-time Super Bowl champion to swiftly return and ensure his side streaked clear in the second half.

Jake Bates made four field goals on a day that was a bit underwhelming for Jared Goff and the Lions' top-ranked offense, which entered averaging 29 points and 395.4 yards per game this season but finished with only 271 total yards.

Goff completed 17 of 25 passes for 170 yards, while being sacked three times as Miami's defense pressured him throughout. He was also intercepted by rookie cornerback Chris Johnson on a tipped pass in the first quarter - just the second pick he has thrown this season.

Jahmyr Gibbs averaged just 3.7 yards per carry, finishing with 74 yards on 20 attempts and an eight-yard rushing score that put the Lions ahead 16-6 entering the fourth quarter.

text:
Los Angeles Rams star wide receiver Puka Nacua went down with a knee injury late in their 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders on Sunday.

Nacua is set to undergo an MRI on Monday to determine the severity of the injury, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter, though the team does not believe that he suffered a torn ACL.

Further specifics, including how long he may be sidelined, are not yet known.

Nacua caught a short pass with about 90 seconds left at Northwest Stadium, but was brought down well short of the line to gain. It didn't appear that anything went wrong in the moment, and Nacua jumped back up and left the field normally after being tackled.

Nacua had 150 yards and a touchdown on 14 catches in the win on Sunday. It marked his third outing this season with at least 125 receiving yards, and he's now scored a touchdown in four of his past five games.

The Rams rallied after falling into an early hole on Sunday to take the seven-point win. Nacua got his touchdown in the fourth quarter of the game on a 7-yard catch from Matthew Stafford, which put them up for good. Nacua somehow managed to make the grab almost through Commanders cornerback Trey Amos in the back of the end zone, too.

While it appears Nacua has avoided a major injury, losing him for any significant amount of time will undoubtedly make things much more difficult for the Rams as they try to mount a playoff push.

They've now won three straight, and will enter next week's matchup with the Arizona Cardinals with a 5-4 record. It's the first time they've been above .500 this fall, too. The Rams do have a bye in Week 11, however, which would give Nacua extra time to recover.

But until his MRI comes back on Monday and the Rams have a clearer picture, his status moving forward is now very much unknown.

title: Panthers DB Faces NFL Punishment for Controversial Hit and Jaylen Waddle Injury
description:
Carolina Panthers cornerback Marco Wilson is a strong candidate for an NFL fine after taunting Denver Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle on Sunday.
The hit that sent Waddle out for a concussion evaluation could draw a separate fine for Panthers safety Zakee Wheatley.
Wilson drew the taunting flag for what he did after the hit.
Jaylen Waddle Injury: WR Being Evaluated For a Concussion After Controversial Hit Denver Post columnist Troy Renck reported that Waddle was being evaluated for a concussion after taking the hit in the second quarter.
Why the NFL Can Still Fine Zakee Wheatley for the Hit The NFL rulebook gives a receiver attempting to catch a pass defenseless-player protection.
text:
Carolina Panthers cornerback Marco Wilson is a strong candidate for an NFL fine after taunting Denver Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle on Sunday. The hit that sent Waddle out for a concussion evaluation could draw a separate fine for Panthers safety Zakee Wheatley.

The distinction is in what the officials called. Wilson drew the taunting flag for what he did after the hit. Wheatley delivered the contact that left Waddle down and then being evalutated for a concussion, and officials did not flag the hit itself.

The flag gives the league a clear basis to review Wilson for unsportsmanlike conduct. The NFL's published fine schedule lists $11,941 for a first taunting offense and $17,911 for a second. The league can adjust those amounts. Earlier this season, it fined Dallas running back Javonte Williams $11,941 for taunting and Chicago receiver Jahdae Walker $5,620 for the same violation, according to the league's accountability report.

Jaylen Waddle Injury: WR Being Evaluated For a Concussion After Controversial Hit

Denver Post columnist Troy Renck reported that Waddle was being evaluated for a concussion after taking the hit in the second quarter. Renck took issue with the contact to Waddle's head and the lack of a flag on the hit. Waddle had left the game with Denver up 10-0.

Waddle had already given Bo Nix one of Denver's biggest gains of the first quarter. He caught a pass for 23 yards to move the Broncos across midfield on the drive that ended with Courtland Sutton's touchdown.

Denver had listed Waddle with a chest injury during the week, but he practiced in full Friday and went into Sunday without an injury designation. The second-quarter hit brought a new concern for a receiver who had scored his second touchdown as a Bronco the previous week against Kansas City.

Why the NFL Can Still Fine Zakee Wheatley for the Hit

The NFL rulebook gives a receiver attempting to catch a pass defenseless-player protection. It also covers a receiver who has completed the catch but hasn't had time to protect himself or clearly become a runner. Among the prohibited forms of contact is a forcible blow to the head or neck with the helmet, facemask, forearm or shoulder.

League officiating staff review every play and can refer potential violations to the compliance team. That means the absence of an unnecessary roughness flag on Wheatley's hit leaves the league free to review the point of contact and Waddle's position at the time. A first offense for hitting a defenseless player carries a listed fine of $17,911.

The NFL and NFLPA singled out hits on defenseless players as one of five safety violations under a tougher repeat-offense policy this season. Three qualifying violations in a season trigger a one-game suspension.

The league typically publishes its weekly fines the following Saturday. Wilson's flag is already on the record. The Week 9 report will show whether the league also takes action on the hit that sent Waddle out of the game.

text:
LANDOVER, Md. -- Los Angeles Rams star receiver Puka Nacua injured his knee on the team's final offensive snap in Sunday's victory over the Washington Commanders, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Mike Garafolo.

Nacua will undergo an MRI on Monday to determine the extent of the injury, the sources said, but the team's initial belief is that he did not suffer a torn ACL.

The injury happened on third down, when Nacua rushed for 5 yards. Nacua took a hard hit on the play and briefly stayed on the ground before walking off the field.

Nacua was not asked about the knee injury after the game. He was asked about his trip to the blue medical tent in the third quarter and said he was checked for a concussion but was cleared.

Nacua had 14 catches for 150 yards and a touchdown in the win. He was targeted 19 times by quarterback Matthew Stafford, who remains without his other top receiving option, Davante Adams (hamstring).

Nacua's 25 receptions over the last two games are the second most by a Rams player in the Super Bowl era, according to ESPN Research. In the two-game span, the next-closest Rams players in terms of receptions are Tutu Atwell, Colby Parkinson and Kyren Williams with four each.

It was Nacua's ninth career regular-season game with at least 150 receiving yards, breaking a tie with Jerry Rice and Randy Moss for the second most by a player within his first four seasons since the 1970 merger.

McVay did have an injury update after the game on tight end Terrance Ferguson, who was expected to return from an ankle injury for the game against the Commanders.

Ferguson, a 2025 second-round pick, pulled his hamstring in practice on Friday.

"You can't make it up, can you?" McVay said.

McVay said it will not "probably be another couple [of] weeks" before Ferguson can return. The Rams started Ferguson's 21-day practice window last week.

"When he got the scan on Friday, it showed he pulled his hamstring," McVay said. "... His ankle was feeling good, though he had a really good work week. He was going to be a big part of the plan today."

title: NFL Week 9 Winners and Losers: Puka Nacua saves the Rams, but now he's dealing with a ...
description:

Even if Nacua avoided a serious injury, the Rams have to know that they can't play like they did Sunday, without anyone else contributing in the passing game.
In the third quarter Stafford forced a pass into Nacua despite Nacua being bracketed closely.
Here are the rest of the winners and losers from Week 9 of the NFL season: WINNERS Tank Dell: The feel-good touchdown of the NFL might have happened Sunday in Los Angeles.
That was a big turning point in a 26-21 Broncos win.
text:
Puka Nacua is great. He is doing things early in his career that have never been matched.

The fatal flaw for the Los Angeles Rams might end up being that Nacua is all they have in the passing game. And now his health is in question.

Nacua was phenomenal again Sunday in a grind-it-out 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders. He had 14 catches for 150 yards on 19 targets with the go-ahead touchdown in the fourth quarter. Nacua also ran it twice for 20 yards. Nobody else on the Rams had more than 20 yards receiving. Nacua had 150 receiving yards and everyone else combined had 78. That's not an ideal formula, no matter how incredible Nacua is as a player.

And then after the game there was some alarming news. Nacua will undergo an MRI on his knee, according to ESPN. The team doesn't believe he has a torn ACL, the report said, but having an MRI means the team has some level of concern.

The results of that test could lead the Rams to get more aggressive at the trade deadline, which is Tuesday. Even if Nacua avoided a serious injury, the Rams have to know that they can't play like they did Sunday, without anyone else contributing in the passing game.

The Rams weren't completely whole in Week 9. They played without cornerback Trent McDuffie and tight end Terrance Ferguson, among others. Davante Adams is out with a hamstring injury and could be out until late in the season, which is why the Rams have so few options at receiver. But they had Myles Garrett back. And Garrett, like Nacua, was great. He had three sacks, including a big 12-yard sack with the game still in doubt late in the fourth quarter. Los Angeles' defense held on, getting a stop on the final play in Rams territory.

Like LA, every team in the NFL is dealing with injuries. The San Francisco 49ers, who lead the NFC West, can attest to that. The Rams just haven't been what everyone thought they would be yet, even though they are getting wins against overmatched teams.

But they are 5-4, which is why the trade deadline is very important for them. Los Angeles has already sold some of its future on trades for Garrett and McDuffie, and it's a team that probably needs another move or two to get back to the status of Super Bowl favorite, particularly at receiver which could be a pressing need if Nacua misses time. Even with him, the Rams have only one option in the passing game.

In the third quarter Stafford forced a pass into Nacua despite Nacua being bracketed closely. Safety Nick Cross had an easy interception. It was a clear case of Stafford forcing it to his only receiver option. It was Stafford's ninth interception this season, surpassing last season's total. That type of play showed why the over-reliance on Nacua in the passing game needs to be addressed.

It doesn't help that Stafford is dealing with an elbow injury. He has not been able to complete passes downfield in Los Angeles' past few games. It could be argued that the Rams having one option at receiver and playing three tight ends more than half of their plays is what's sapping the offense of its explosiveness, but Stafford's elbow doesn't help either. LA's longest play Sunday, against a bad Washington defense, was 21 yards.

Perhaps Adams returns from a serious injury and fills the Rams' need, but that's a gamble for a receiver who will turn 34 on Dec. 24. It also assumes Nacua, who has a long history of injuries and is taking a lot of punishment with all of the touches he's receiving, doesn't get bad news on the MRI or that he stays healthy the rest of the season even if this injury scare isn't bad. If Nacua misses time, the Rams' passing game will be in trouble.

The Rams can celebrate their third straight win after a disappointing 2-4 start, but with some concern over one of their most important players. It's clear they need to be making calls before Tuesday's trade deadline if they want to reach their peak this season. And it could reach a critical level based on Nacua's MRI.

Here are the rest of the winners and losers from Week 9 of the NFL season:

WINNERS

Tank Dell: The feel-good touchdown of the NFL might have happened Sunday in Los Angeles.

Tank Dell hadn't scored since 2024. He missed all of last season with a horrific leg injury, and had played in just one game this season as he continued to recover. Anyone who had forgotten about Dell was reminded of him when he caught a long pass from C.J. Stroud and was running down the sideline for a 63-yard touchdown. That set off a celebration on the Texans' sideline. It was a great moment for Dell, whose career had been in doubt after he tore multiple ligaments in his knee and also suffered a dislocated kneecap.

The Texans got an easy 44-22 win over a Chargers team that is 0-8 and somehow getting worse as the season goes on. Stroud was fantastic on Sunday with 384 yards and five touchdowns. The defense got to Justin Herbert often, forcing him into another rough game. Houston had eight sacks. It was a good win, but will be remembered for Dell's long touchdown, which sealed his comeback from injury.

Drew Lock: At very least, Lock is establishing himself as a reliable backup quarterback. That can lead to a lot of contracts and a long career.

Lock has been called upon to start twice this season and has done his job each time. He had a steady game for the Seattle Seahawks, which was without Sam Darnold due to a quad injury, not turning it over once. That's a perfectly fine formula for the Seahawks, who rely on their defense. With Lock doing enough on offense, the defense clamped down on the Arizona Cardinals and won 17-3.

Lock had 175 yards and a touchdown in the win. He wasn't spectacular. But he didn't make any big mistakes and played an important role in a win, which is all any team asks of its backup quarterback.

The Broncos and their good fortune: Denver is catching every break this season. It simply can't lose in one-score games.

The Broncos were trailing 14-13 and the Carolina Panthers had first-and-goal at the 1-yard line when they got one of the most fortunate interceptions you'll see, and it turned the game around. The Panthers decided to throw on first-and-goal. The pass was heading for the ground only to be tipped in the air by tight end Tommy Tremble. Broncos safety Devon Key made a great play to realize the ball was still live and pluck it out of the air before it hit the ground. A challenge and a review showed it was a clean interception. That was a big turning point in a 26-21 Broncos win.

The Broncos got going after that. They scored two straight touchdowns to take a two-score lead.

But Denver doesn't play easy games. Carolina scored and then forced a punt after a pitch to Broncos running back Jonah Coleman was fumbled for a big loss. Denver eventually hit Bryce Young, who fumbled, and the Broncos recovered with 1:15 to go. It was another win for the Broncos, their 16th in a row in one-score games. That sets an NFL record which they tied last week when they held on in the final seconds against the Chiefs. The Broncos are 7-2, and piling up wins in close games. Per usual, they had some serendipity on their side.

Jameis Winston: He didn't start Sunday but came up with the key drive the New York Giants needed to get past the Philadelphia Eagles.

Winston came in when J.J. McCarthy briefly left the game after taking a hard hit to his side. Winston got one full drive and made it count. On the drive he completed 6-of-7 passes for 71 yards and a touchdown to Isaiah Likely. Winston also ran for 11 yards.

Offense was a struggle for the Giants all game but Winston did his job. It was the Giants' only touchdown in a 19-11 win, their first road win at Philadelphia since 2013. They improved to 5-2-1.

Winston was benched for McCarthy as the Giants chase a division title in the terrible NFC East. But he might have been their most important player Sunday, coming through when nothing else was working for New York's offense.

Kenneth Walker III: After a couple of quiet games against very good defenses, Walker got an easier assignment Sunday. And he took advantage of it.

Walker scored two touchdowns on catches and another on the ground as the Chiefs' offense broke out in a 35-12 win over the New York Jets. He rushed for 102 yards and had another 41 receiving. It hadn't been easy for the Chiefs on the road against the Seahawks and Broncos the past two weeks, and Walker in particular was stymied. He was on a blistering pace early in the season but had just 105 rushing yards and no touchdowns the past two weeks. On Sunday he was back to his form of the first few weeks when he was getting buzz as a potential MVP candidate. The Chiefs are 6-2, and still very much in the mix for an AFC West title as long as Walker continues to play well.

Joe Burrow for MVP: The Atlanta Falcons were one of Burrow's toughest matchups in November. All he did was go 18-of-22 passing for 239 yards with two touchdowns, and one rushing TD. And that was just the first half.

Burrow's MVP push continued Sunday in Madrid as he finished with 271 passing yards and three touchdown passes in a 34-17 win over the Atlanta Falcons. He probably could have put up even bigger numbers but the Bengals were up double digits for most of the second half. The NFL Network broadcast repeatedly talked about how Burrow told them in production meetings how confident he feels and how healthy he is. It shows.

The Bengals are 6-2 and in good shape to win the AFC North, which is usually a prerequisite for winning MVP. He is putting up monster numbers. He hasn't won before and there will be some sentiment to recognize him with his first MVP award as he turns 30 years old. By the end of November he could be the clear favorite, though Josh Allen, Brock Purdy and Caleb Williams are also in the race. But Burrow is looking like the league's MVP.

LOSERS

Patriots secondary: The Green Bay Packers had a receiver go for 164 yards and a touchdown on Sunday, and it wasn't even the biggest receiving performance on his own team. That's how bad New England's defense was Sunday.

The Packers made it clear where the ball was going. It was either heading to Matthew Golden or Christian Watson, and usually deep. New England did nothing to stop it. Golden and Watson ran wide open in the Patriots' defensive backfield all game and Jordan Love kept piling up yards in a 45-27 win in New England.

Love was so good he was pulled early in the fourth quarter, with the Packers cruising to a blowout win. He had 372 yards and three touchdowns, riding his two red-hot receivers.

Watson had 171 receiving yards and a touchdown. Golden had 164 yards and a touchdown, including 126 yards in the first quarter.

The Packers are 6-3, and have completely turned things around since a sluggish first month of the season. Their combination of Love throwing to Golden and Watson has been devastating. Ask the Patriots, who are usually a solid defensive team. On Sunday, it was like they weren't even on the field against the Packers.

Raiders offense: The scoreboard didn't reflect it, but the Las Vegas Raiders had a chance to at least make the San Francisco 49ers sweat on the second half Sunday. But they turned it over five times after halftime.

The Raiders had six possessions in the second half and one turned out well, with a touchdown. The other five ended with three Kirk Cousins interceptions, one of which was returned for a pick-6 and another that was thrown into the end zone with the Raiders inside the 5-yard line. There were also two fumbles, one of which came right before tight end Michael Mayer was about to score, which would have cut San Francisco's lead to 28-24. The Raiders went on to lose 38-17.

The 49ers' defense played well, as it has all season, and that's a big reason San Francisco is 7-1. But on Sunday, the Raiders played their sloppiest half of the season. It's hard to turn it over five times in one half, but Las Vegas somehow pulled it off.

Malik Willis: The whole season is a tryout for Willis, who has to prove he's worthy of being the Miami Dolphins' quarterback of the future. Sunday wasn't a good day for him.

Facing a Detroit Lions defense that isn't good and was down multiple starters due to injury, the Dolphins never reached the end zone. Willis was inaccurate on many passes. The Lions were surprisingly quiet on offense too but it didn't matter. Miami couldn't score enough to keep up and lost 19-9. Willis was 13-of-25 passing for 128 yards and an interception against a Lions defense that was 29th in yards per game allowed coming in.

Willis has had decent moments, and he has to be graded on a curve because of the lack of talent around him. But he wasn't good enough Sunday.

Deshaun Watson: Shedeur Sanders couldn't come up with the two-point conversion he needed to close out the win over the New Orleans Saints. But he might have given the Browns a reason to consider a quarterback change.

Sanders, who threw a go-ahead 64-yard touchdown to KC Concepcion late in the fourth quarter and also led a game-tying field goal drive in the final seconds of regulation, hit tight end Harold Fannin Jr. for a 39-yard touchdown in overtime after the New Orleans Saints scored first, with Fannin making a great play after the catch. But Sanders threw incomplete on the two-point conversion that would have won the game (there was also a holding call on the Browns) and the New Orleans Saints held on to a 23-22 win.

The loss stung but Sanders played well, as Watson sat out due to being in the concussion protocol during the week. Watson has mostly played poorly and the Browns have been winning in spite of it. Sanders had 297 yards and two touchdowns against the Saints with multiple clutch drives. It will at least be worth considering a change after that.

Sauce Gardner: Gardner's presence on the Indianapolis Colts is a constant reminder of the collapse of the franchise.

Last season, when the Colts were 7-2, Indianapolis traded two first-round picks and receiver Adonai Mitchell for Gardner, an elite cornerback. But Gardner has been mostly hurt with the Colts, who have fallen apart since the middle of last season. And on Sunday, with a chance to beat the Dallas Cowboys, Gardner got beat for the biggest play of the game.

Ryan Flournoy, playing a bigger role with George Pickens out, beat Gardner for a 46-yard catch late in the game when the Colts led 23-20. That set up a go-ahead rushing touchdown from Javonte Williams and the Cowboys defense closed out the win when rookie safety Caleb Downs picked off Daniel Jones, who had another rough day. Dallas held on for a 27-23 win.

The Colts' fall is far from Gardner's fault, but he hasn't helped and the Colts paid way too much for him. Him giving up the game-changing catch to Flournoy was just another reminder of how costly that trade was.

text:
The New York Giants appear to have survived another injury scare at the quarterback position. J.J. McCarthy returned to Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles after spending time in the sideline medical tent and locker room while being evaluated for a hip injury.

With McCarthy initially deemed questionable to return, the Giants turned back to Jameis Winston, who started four games before McCarthy replaced him atop the depth chart. Winston led a touchdown drive before he headed back to the sideline.

McCarthy took a hard hit to his lower abdomen on a quarterback keeper in the third quarter. Eagles linebacker Zack Baun led with his helmet while attempting to stop McCarthy's run and made contact with McCarthy's side on the tackle.

McCarthy attempted to throw on the sideline before heading to the locker room and was in obvious pain after he completed his throwing motion. He grabbed at his side and fell to the turf as medical staff came to his assistance. Despite the clear discomfort, he was able to get back into game action just before the end of the quarter.

The Giants were mostly quiet on offense during McCarthy's Week 9 start and scored only six points before he left with the injury. McCarthy was 9-for-13 for 101 passing yards and ran three times for another 11 yards ahead of his brief exit.

Although it seems that McCarthy will remain in action beyond this week, if the injury acts up on him and forces him to miss time, his potential absence may be a significant blow to the NFC East-leading Giants. Already without Jaxson Dart for the rest of the year due to the torn knee ligaments he suffered in Week 2, New York traded for McCarthy as a potential season-long solution. His effectiveness upon insertion into the lineup in the fourth quarter of the Week 6 loss to the New Orleans Saints and in his first start the following week came as a pleasant surprise and gave the Giants reason to believe they could maintain their division lead.

J.J. McCarthy departed Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles in the third quarter after taking a hard hit. McCarthy suffered the injury after he scrambled for a short gain, with Eagles linebacker Zack Baun hitting from behind.

McCarthy didn't express immediate pain, but he went to the Giants' sideline for the next snap. He attempted to throw a pass while trainers evaluated him. But Winston was benched after struggling during his fourth start of the season. Winston has thrown for 957 yards, seven touchdowns and five interceptions this season, going 2-1-1 in the games he's started.

McCarthy, meanwhile, threw for 495 yards, a touchdown and an interception prior to Sunday's game. He completed 9 of 13 passes for 101 yards prior to leaving Sunday's game. The Giants trailed the Eagles 8-6 when McCarthy got hurt.

text:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- Broncos wide receiver Jaylen Waddle and cornerback Riley Moss sustained concussions within minutes of each other in Denver's 26-21 victory over the Carolina Panthers on Sunday.

The Broncos went into the game without either of their starting safeties as Brandon Jones (hamstring) and Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) were both game-day inactives.

Second-year cornerback Jahdae Barron played in Moss' spot. Moss was injured as he made a tackle on Trevor Etienne in the second quarter.

Waddle, who had one catch Sunday for 22 yards, left the game with seconds to go in the first quarter. He reached to make a catch in front of Panthers cornerback Marco Wilson and was hit by Zakee Wheatley, who knocked the ball free.

Waddle, who has battled ankle and chest injuries already this season, jumped up after the play and walked toward the Broncos huddle but then left the field and did not return. He has 30 receptions for 337 yards and two touchdowns this season.

text:
Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes left Sunday's game against the New York Jets with an injury scare after a hit to his throwing elbow but was able to return to help lead a 35-12 win.

The hit took place in the second quarter on a sack that forced a fumble. Mahomes' right elbow bent awkwardly on the sack, and he fumbled the ball. He was in clear pain after the hit and walked to the sideline holding his right arm. The Jets took over possession after recovering the fumble.

But Mahomes was able to throw on the sideline and returned to the field before the end of the half after the Chiefs retook possession of the ball.

Kansas City took over with 32 seconds remaining in the half after a missed Jets field goal and Mahomes was able to complete a 12-yard pass, then scramble for seven yards to set up a Harrison Butker field-goal attempt just before the end of the half.

Butker missed the 51-yard attempt, and the Chiefs went into halftime with a 14-12 lead.

"He hurt his elbow a little bit," head coach Andy Reid told CBS at halftime. "It's sore, but he came back. He's a tough kid."

Mahomes continued to play to start the third quarter and led the Chiefs to a touchdown drive on their first possession of the half to extend their lead to 21-12. The Jets didn't mount a challenge from there.

Mahomes didn't appear to be impacted by the injury scare and finished the day completing 230of-31 passes for 278 yards (7.8 yards per attempt) with 2 touchdowns and no turnovers.

"If I'm able to play, I'm going to play," Mahomes said after the game. "In scares you in moments when you get pains in certains areas of your body, so obviously I didn't feel great. I was able to get it worked on a little bit, especially at halftime, and was able to go out there and play the rest of the game."

Mahomes said he felt good after the game. "I'm sure I'll be sore tomorrow, but we'll get right to it and work on it."

The Chiefs improved to 6-2 with the win and remain a half game in the AFC West behind the Denver Broncos, who improved to 7-2 with a 26-21 win over the Carolina Panthers.

If he missed nine weeks, that could allow Jackson to return in early January for the regular-season finale against the Steelers — and anything that followed in the playoffs for the 4-5 Ravens who’ve now lost four consecutive games following a 4-1 start to the 2026 campaign.

They also have a pair of games on Dec. 27 and 31 against the Browns and Bengals in Weeks 16 and 17, respectively.

The Ravens placed Jackson — who has thrown for 967 yards and six touchdowns this season, while rushing for another 144 yards and a touchdown — on injured reserve, but he wasn’t ruled out for the season and would be eligible to return.

When Jackson spoke with his teammates, he was “energizing” and “exciting,” according to ESPN.

When the hand of Bills outside linebacker Greg Rousseau connected with Jackson’s right thumb, it marked another devastating injury blow to the Ravens this season — and marked just the start of more quarterback chaos.

Tyler Huntley, who entered for Jackson in Buffalo, exited in the second quarter with a season-ending turf toe injury, leaving third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano to finish the loss to the Bills and start their loss to the Jaguars on Thursday.

INDIANAPOLIS -- The Dallas Cowboys will be without wide receiver George Pickens, cornerback Joey Porter Jr. and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown on Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts.

Pickens (shoulder, hamstring), Porter (ankle) and Overshown (back) had been listed as questionable Friday after being limited last week in practice.

Pickens has been bothered by a shoulder injury since the Cowboys' Oct. 8 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. His hamstring injury has been an issue the past two weeks and limited his work in practice.

Porter has had ankle issues for the past few weeks and was unable to finish last week's loss against the Arizona Cardinals.

Overshown's back injury flared up this week, and he has been dealing with a hamstring issue. He spent time on injured reserve after suffering a hamstring injury in Dallas' season opener against the Giants.

Pickens has 39 catches for 533 yards and two touchdowns, off the pace he had a year ago, when he had 93 catches for 1,429 yards and nine scores in his first year with the Cowboys. Porter, who was acquired by the Cowboys on Oct. 1 from the Pittsburgh Steelers, will have missed two full games because of injury/illness. He was sent home after arriving at AT&T Stadium with flu-like symptoms before the Cowboys' loss to the Buccaneers. He has been credited with eight tackles, a tackle for loss and three pass breakups in the four games he has played.

The Cowboys will have Ryan Flournoy move into the No. 2 wide receiver role opposite CeeDee Lamb, while Jonathan Mingo will be the No. 3 receiver. The Cowboys will be without KaVontae Turpin (ribs) for the third straight game and have undrafted rookies Camden Brown and Jordan Hudson available.

Cobie Durant is likely to replace Porter. He started Dallas' first two games before suffering a hamstring injury. Shavon Revel Jr., who was inactive last week, will play.

text:
The Detroit Lions took the field in Week 9 against the Miami Dolphins without a key member of their defense – Jack Campbell.

It marks the Lions' first contest since the linebacker suffered a terrifying neck injury during the team's Week 8 win over the Minnesota Vikings. The injury left Campbell laying on the field motionless before being carted off the field on a backboard as emotional teammates looked on.

Campbell issued a statement about his condition on Wednesday, Nov. 4. He said that he has movement in his lower body and was making progress towards regaining movement in his upper body. It was an encouraging update that extended beyond the generic ones provided earlier in the week.

On Nov. 7, the Lions announced they were placing the linebacker on injured reserve. It's a reminder that Campbell has a long way to go in his recovery, but he remains determined to get back on the field, according to CBS Sports' Melanie Collins.

"He is determined to get back on this football field, telling Dan Campbell: 'Just make sure the house is taken care of until I can get back,'" Collins reported on the CBS broadcast of the game.

As for his teammates, they are back to work without him. Here's what to know about Campbell and the latest on his condition.

Is Jack Campbell still in the hospital?

Campbell remains hospitalized, but continues to improve, according to CBS Sports' Melanie Collins. Collins said on the pregame broadcast that Campbell said that while he doesn't want any tears or sympathy, he does want to get back on the field.

Campbell on Wednesday, Nov. 4, thanked his caregivers at Henry Ford Hospital in Detroit and the Detroit Lions medical staff.

Lions wear Jack Campbell's jersey to Week 9 game

Several Lions players honored Campbell ahead of the team's Week 9 contest by wearing his jersey to Hard Rock Stadium – home of the Miami Dolphins.

Linebackers Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez and K.J. Britt were among the players wearing Campbell's jersey. Kelvin Sheppard, the Lions defensive coordinator, also sported the No. 46 jersey.

Check out the photos:

What is Jack Campbell's condition?

Campbell announced in a statement on Nov. 4 that he has full movement in his lower body. He is continuing to make progress with movement in his upper body.

It was the first concrete update on Campbell's condition since the injury occurred on Sunday, Nov. 1. Prior to Campbell's statement, the team had issued more general updates, saying that preliminary results were positive.

Is Jack Campbell paralyzed?

Campbell appears to have avoided the worst fears that immediately followed his injury, as his updates indicate that he has avoided full paralysis from the neck down. Campbell said he has "full movement in my lower body" and was working to regain upper-body movement as part of his recovery.

Latest Jack Campbell injury update

Jack Campbell has been placed on injured reserve, the Lions announced on Nov. 7.

The linebacker announced in a statement on Nov. 4 that he has full movement in his lower body and is continuing to make progress with movement in his upper body.

Dan Campbell previously provided small update on Jack Campbell's status during a Tuesday, Nov. 3, radio appearance on 97.1 The Ticket.

"It's not easy because he's always going to be on our minds over here," Dan Campbell said of Jack Campbell, when addressing the Lions' preparation for Week 9. "The good news is he is improving."

The Lions coach made it clear he is providing his players with updates about Jack Campbell's status through the team's captains.

"I think the thought of him – knowing he's doing better, and I've kept the captains up to date, and they've let the other guys know its good news," Dan Campbell said, referencing how players were reacting to the situation. "I think that helps everybody just get a better handle on all this."

Campbell also added that he is trying to keep his players focused on their upcoming game against the Miami Dolphins, expressing concern that "bad things can happen" if players aren't able to be all-in on their gameday responsibilities.

What happened to Jack Campbell?

Campbell went down with a neck injury after tackling Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson.

He stayed down as the training staff and medical personnel surrounded him and a cart arrived. Campbell was loaded onto a backboard before the cart took him off the field. He was transported to a local hospital to be evaluated for a neck injury after exiting the team's Week 8 win over the Vikings.

The Lions announced late Sunday night that Campbell was resting and was scheduled to remain in a local hospital overnight for continued evaluation and monitoring.

Jack Campbell statement

Jack Campbell issued a statement, via the Lions' X account on Nov. 4. Here it is, in its entirety:

My family and I want to sincerely thank everyone for the overwhelming amount of love, prayers, and support we’ve received over the past few days. It means more to us than words can express.

I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body. I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better.

My faith in God has never been stronger. I know He has a plan for me, and I trust in that plan. I know there may be challenges ahead, but with my faith, my family, and so many people in my corner, I know we’ll get through this.

I especially want to thank the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded and cared for me on the field. I know those were difficult moments, and I’m incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me. The way you handled everything and looked after me when I needed it most is something I’ll never forget. From the bottom of my heart, thank you.

I also can’t say enough about the incredible care I’ve received from the medical team at Henry Ford Hospital and the Detroit Lions medical staff. They’ve been amazing to me and my family throughout this process, and I’m truly grateful for everything they’ve done.

To my teammates, coaches, and everyone in the Lions organization, I want you to know how much I love and appreciate you. This team is a family to me, and the way everyone has been there for me means everything. I’m proud to be a Detroit Lion and couldn’t ask to be surrounded by a better group of people.

One thing I’ve learned about Detroit is that this city is built on toughness, resilience, and grit. That’s exactly how I’m going to approach this challenge.

Please continue to keep me and my family in your prayers. We feel the love, and I can’t thank everyone enough.

God is good. My faith is strong.

Jack Campbell

Who is Jack Campbell?

Campbell is a linebacker for the Detroit Lions.

The 26-year-old is in his fourth NFL season, all with Detroit. The Lions drafted Campbell with the 18th overall pick in the first round of the 2023 NFL Draft after he starred in college for the Iowa Hawkeyes.

A native of Cedar Falls, Iowa, Campbell broke out during his junior season with the Hawkeyes, totaling 143 tackles, two interceptions, two fumble recoveries and a sack in 2021. Returning for his senior season, Campbell was named an All-American in 2022 and received the Butkus Award as the top linebacker in college football.

He also received the William V. Campbell Trophy, also known as the "academic Heisman," in 2022 for being recognized as the college football player with the best combination of academics, leadership and on-field performance.

Campbell slid right in as a key piece of the Lions' defense after arriving in the NFL. However, he didn't officially break out until his third season. Campbell recorded 176 total tackles, three forced fumbles and five sacks en route to being named a first-team All-Pro and earning his first Pro Bowl appearance last season.

On May 21, 2026, the Lions recognized Campbell's breakout with a four-year, $81 million extension.

Jack Campbell to receive Iowa game ball

The former Hawkeye was honored by his former head coach, Kirk Ferentz, after Iowa's win over Northwestern on Nov. 7, when it was announced that Campbell would receive a game ball.

“All the feedback has been really positive,” Ferentz said, via HawkCentral, part of the USA TODAY Network. “Hearing some encouraging news, it’s going to be an – I don’t know how long road – but it’s moving in the right direction. Thought that was really fitting certainly to give him a ball and we’ll get that to him.”

Ferentz quickly joked that it was a good thing Iowa took care of business with a 24-10 win, since the alternative could've ruined the moment.

“Glad we won, cause otherwise you’re kind of screwed, ya know?” Ferentz joked. “Screws everything up.”

Eric Larsen contributed to this report.

The Detroit Lions are letting linebacker Jack Campbell know he is in their thoughts. A week after Campbell was carted off the field and hospitalized, multiple members of the Lions showed up for Sunday's game wearing his jersey.

The team shared a few images prior to its Week 9 game against the Miami Dolphins.

Campbell was stretchered off the field after making a tackle during the team's Week 8 game against the Minnesota Vikings. It was clear immediately Campbell had sustained a significant injury on the play, as his arms went limp and he lay motionless on the field. Eventually, the entire Lions team came out and knelt around Campbell. Some members of the team were emotional. He was later ruled out with a neck injury.

The linebacker was taken to a local hospital and was said to be making positive progress early in the week. On Wednesday, he released a statement of his own, saying he had movement in his lower body and was "continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body."

Campbell, who is in his fourth year with the team, was off to a strong start after making the All-Pro team last season. Through seven games, he had 57 combined tackles prior to the injury.

title: Mitch Albom: After injuries like Jack Campbell's, a question remains - Detroit Free Press
description:
The Lions medical team literally had to bring him back to life, and he, too, was initially paralyzed.
And I have found myself, after each awful incident, asking the same question: Should we still be playing this sport?
It's entertainment We all know NFL football is tremendously violent and wildly dangerous.
There are many nations that don’t play football and some cultures that would find it violent to the point of illegality.
So do football players like Campbell.
text:
Last Sunday at Ford Field, when Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell went down on what seemed like a routine tackle, and he didn’t get up, and he still didn’t get up, and his inert body on the turf resembled a man who had been dropped from a plane, I was, like many of you, stunned and saddened.

But I also flashed back to another game, in the Pontiac Silverdome 35 years ago, when Lions offensive lineman Mike Utley, on a touchdown pass, lost his balance during the block and was driven into the turf at a horrific angle, causing his head to snap back and leaving him paralyzed from the neck down.

I then realized both tragedies occurred on the first play of the fourth quarter, and I flashed back once again, this time to 1997, another fourth quarter at the Silverdome, when Lions linebacker Reggie Brown went to tackle a New York Jets running back and collided with another Jets lineman right at the head and the neck.

Brown stopped breathing. His esophagus locked. His lips turned blue. The Lions medical team literally had to bring him back to life, and he, too, was initially paralyzed. He eventually recovered, but his NFL career was done.

He was 23.

In all three cases, the reaction was the same. A hush over a previously raucous crowd. Players shaking their heads, fighting back tears, on their knees in prayer. TV announcers dropping their voices to somber-toned declarations about “we hope he will be all right” and “this is the hard part of football.”

And in each case, after a stretch of time, the player was carted off to cheers from the home crowd. The broadcast came back from commercials.

And play resumed.

Three Lions. Similar fates. And I have found myself, after each awful incident, asking the same question: Should we still be playing this sport?

It's entertainment

We all know NFL football is tremendously violent and wildly dangerous. We also know it’s optional. It isn’t firefighting, a perilous job necessary to society.

No, the NFL is entertainment. One of the richest forms of entertainment in the world. Hundreds of millions of viewers around the globe, a Super Bowl that is the single biggest sports night in America. Players get paid crazy salaries, with quarterbacks now earning north of $60 million a year.

But it’s not mandatory. There are many nations that don’t play football and some cultures that would find it violent to the point of illegality.

Which leads you to play this game in your head: If football didn’t exist, Jack Campbell would be walking today, Mike Utley would be walking today, Darryl Stingley would not have been a quadriplegic, countless players wouldn’t have spent their older years with issues related to CTE (chronic traumatic encephalopathy) or have died as a result of them.

Then again, if the world had banned boxing, Benny Paret, Kim Duk-koo, Davey Moore and Maxim Dadashev might still be alive, instead of dying shortly after fights with severe brain injuries.

And if they banned race car driving, Dale Earnhardt and Ayrton Senna might still be with us, instead of dying in crashes.You can go on and on. Professional bull riding. Mixed martial arts. No sport, no death from the sport.So why does that never get raised when a horrific scene like Campbell going down last Sunday happens?

The price they pay

It doesn’t get raised because the athletes and coaches are never the ones raising it. It’s always someone from the outside. A spine specialist. A neurosurgeon.

When Dr. Bennet Omalu, a Nigerian-born forensic pathologist and neuropathologist, first discovered CTE in American football players in 2002, the NFL’s response — instead of being, “Wow, we need to step back and make changes” —was to discredit him for years and attack his research.

That’s because the business of football has always been a bigger concern to owners than the casualties of it. But you can’t lay the blame solely on them.

The fact is, virtually all the men playing in the NFL want to be there. They know the risks. Or they believe they know the risks. Maybe they think it won’t happen to them. And maybe they think differently when it does.

Or maybe not. Utley, 25 years after his injury, told the media at his College Football Hall of Fame ceremony, "I miss [football] tremendously, and I would go do it all over again even though I'm sitting in here a crippled dude."

A different breed

Football has often been likened to the Roman gladiators, who often fought to the death to the pleasure of crowds. There are similarities. Cheers for hits. Louder cheers for bigger hits. But did you know that every gladiator had to take an oath before joining the fraternity: "To endure to be burned, to be bound, to be beaten, and to be killed by the sword"?

In other words, they knew what they were getting into. So do football players like Campbell. You rewatch that scene of him flat on Ford Field, you read about his college sweetheart wife and their 4-month-old baby, and your heart breaks, and you maybe you say, “If only he hadn’t played football.”

But I don’t think he says it.

These NFL guys are not the same breed as the rest of us. Same for race car drivers and boxers. A reporter once asked Mike Tyson why he was coming back to boxing after numerous controversies, declining skills, and continued risks to his body and head.

“I’m a fighter,” he said, simply. “A fighter fights.”

His choice. Campbell’s choice. And our choice to watch or turn away.

With 14 games remaining in NFL Week 9, the injury landscape is creating massive ripples across the betting markets. Shifting point spreads and fluctuating player props mean staying ahead of official game designations is your best bet for finding an edge.

The Buffalo Bills have a wild 18 players on their weekly report, while the Philadelphia Eagles have listed six players as out. NFL Week 9 Injury Reports for Star Player

Staying on top of official injury designations is the key to finding closing line value. Above is my roundup of the most-notable star players dealing with injuries ahead of Week 9. I highlighted their practice participation and official game statuses.

49ers: Deebo Samuel & Mike Evans (Hamstring / Ribs)

The 49ers enter Week 9 with their perimeter passing attack decimated, as both Deebo Samuel Sr. (hamstring) and Mike Evans (ribs) have been officially ruled out after failing to practice. The combined loss of these two star wideouts creates a staggering statistical vacuum, vacating nearly 48% of San Francisco’s total target share, over 55% of the team’s air yards, and the overwhelming majority of their manufactured touches behind the line of scrimmage and in the red zone.

From a betting perspective, this dual absence completely lowers the ceiling of San Francisco’s offense, triggering sharp movement toward the full-game under and a noticeable drop in the 49ers’ implied team total. Without Samuel’s elite yards-after-catch versatility on jet sweeps and screen concepts, and without Evans’ dominant contested-catch presence along the boundary and in goal-to-go situations, Kyle Shanahan’s play-calling will naturally contract.

In the prop market, this forces extreme volume consolidation onto the remaining pass-catchers. Tight end George Kittle and the primary pass-catching running backs project for massive bumps in route participation and third-down target share, making their receptions and receiving yards overs high-priority targets. Conversely, quarterback passing yardage and passing touchdown props become sharp fade opportunities, as San Francisco is heavily incentivized to lean into a conservative, run-heavy script to control clock and protect against negative plays.

Browns: Deshaun Watson (Concussion)

Deshaun Watson is out of concussion protocol and officially listed as questionable but the Browns have already said that Shedeur Sanders will start on Sunday. In the betting market, sportsbooks have kept Cleveland’s spread and total relatively suppressed, pricing in the realistic probability of a backup signal-caller taking the reins in a hostile road environment.

With Watson potentially out, Cleveland’s offensive scheme shifts drastically toward a condensed, low-risk identity built on heavy 12-personnel sets, early-down runs, and short checkdowns to backs and tight ends.

Bettors should anticipate sharp money hammering the under on both Cleveland’s team total and the full-game total if Sanders does start, while wide receiver boundary props become immediate fades against a defense capable of stacking eight men in the box.

Even if Pickens suits up at less than 100%, hamstring soft-tissue limitations severely hinder top-end burst and perimeter separation, making his receiving yards prop (often set in the mid-to-high 60s) a prime candidate for an under. If he is declared inactive or placed on a restricted snap count, the entire distribution of the passing game shifts inward. CeeDee Lamb’s target floor skyrockets into double-digit territory, while tight end and running back underneath reception props become high-value overs against a Colts secondary that will pivot toward bracketing Lamb.

Losing Pickens’ ability to stretch the field horizontally lowers Dallas’ explosive-play rate, reducing the likelihood of quick-strike scores and favoring a more methodical, clock-draining game script.

DeVonta Smith’s hamstring injury completely reshapes Philadelphia’s offensive target distribution in their rivalry clash with the Giants. Vacating a 22.4% target share and over 35% of the team’s air yards, Smith’s absence removes Philadelphia’s premier vertical intermediate separator on the boundary.

In the prop market, this creates immediate, high-leverage volume consolidation. Dallas Goedert sees his intermediate usage surge from 16.4% to over 24%, making Goedert’s receptions and anytime touchdown props priority targets. Furthermore, with fewer spread-out boundary concepts stretching the defense, expect Philadelphia to lean into a run-heavy, ball-control script behind Saquon Barkley, suppressing full-game passing totals.

Patriots: A.J. Brown (Ankle)

Brown being ruled out with an ankle injury strips New England of its unquestioned WR1 and primary explosive play threat. Brown accounts for a massive portion of the Patriots’ contested-catch equity and vertical passing yardage, serving as the focal point opposing defensive coordinators build their entire coverage game plans around.

Without Brown drawing bracket coverage on the boundary, opposing secondaries can comfortably drop an extra safety into the box to clog early-down rushing lanes and choke intermediate passing windows. The betting ripple effect is swift: New England’s implied team total suffers a significant downgrade, deep passing yardage props become instant under candidates, and the offense is forced into slow, methodical drive structures that strongly favor full-game unders.

Vikings: Kyler Murray (Hamstring)

Kyler Murray being ruled out with a hamstring strain removes the central engine of the Minnesota offense, completely recalibrating both the side and total markets. Minnesota will turn to Carson Wentz on Monday night as the Vikings host the Bills.

text:
Lamar Jackson's latest injury has sidetracked the Ravens' 2026 season, leaving them to trade for journeyman Jacoby Brissett this week amid a 4-5 start.

But the two-time MVP may not be lost for the year.

The Baltimore signal-caller suffered a fractured and dislocated thumb on his right hand, and is expected to miss at least six weeks after undergoing surgery, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Sunday. Jackson could miss up to nine weeks with his recovery, which would put his return to play around the start of the postseason at the latest, if the Ravens make it that far.

Rapoport reported that Jackson told his teammates after Week 8 that he plans to return later this season. The Ravens QB was initially reported to be out indefinitely.

With Jackson and Tyler Huntley (out for the season with turf toe) placed on injured reserve, the Ravens were forced to start undrafted third-stringer Joe Fagnano on Thursday night against Jacksonville. It did not go well.

The Ravens then acquired Brissett on Friday in a trade, with hopes that the veteran QB can lead Baltimore to enough wins in the ensuing weeks to make a Jackson return worthwhile.

Baltimore faces the Chargers, Panthers, Texans and Buccaneers (a combined 8-21 record) in the next five weeks before finishing the season with four games in the brutal AFC North. The Ravens are currently last in the division.

Jackson has started five games this season, his first under coach Jesse Minter, but finished just three. He left Baltimore's Week 4 game with an ankle sprain and missed three weeks. Upon his return in Week 8, Jackson was knocked out of the game on the first snap when his right hand collided with a Bills defender.

On the season, Jackson is 68-of-97 passing for 967 yards, six touchdowns and one interception, adding 144 rushing yards and a TD.

Brissett started all eight of the Cardinals' games before being benched midway through their Week 8 comeback win over Dallas. He was demoted to third string the following day and then dealt to Baltimore.

The 33-year-old journeyman has completed 63.3% of his passes for 1,719 yards, 10 TDs and seven INTs this season.

Brissett will try to keep Baltimore afloat through the winter with the expectation that Jackson can return to a playoff-bound Ravens team and take them over the top.

text:
Cleveland Browns fans spent the week waiting on news from two places: the training room in Berea and the league office in New York. The second answer came Saturday, when NFL Network's Tom Pelissero reported that the league fined Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker $17,911 for the hit that eventually put Deshaun Watson in the concussion protocol.

That's the first-offense amount for roughing the passer. Brisker came free on a blitz three plays into the Browns' 27-6 loss in Pittsburgh and hit Watson high, drawing a flag and sending him to the medical tent.

Brisker's postgame jab aged poorly in Cleveland

Brisker had little sympathy after the game. "Babying the quarterback. He's over there crying or whatever he's doing. It is what it is. He had his binky today," he said, per PennLive.

Watson was cleared by the unaffiliated neurotrauma consultant and returned on the next series. He finished 27 of 39 for 324 yards while being sacked eight times, then passed evaluations after the game and Monday morning. "On Tuesday morning, he reported to the medical staff that he began experiencing concussion symptoms Monday night and was immediately placed in the concussion protocol," the Browns said in a statement released Wednesday.

The fine itself is a small bite. Brisker signed a one-year, $5.5 million deal with Pittsburgh in March, and his base salary of $1,215,000 works out to $67,500 per weekly check over 18 weeks. The league took about a quarter of one of them.

Cleveland is still dealing with the fallout. Watson cleared the protocol and will make the trip, but he's questionable, and Todd Monken named Shedeur Sanders the starter Sunday against the Saints. "He's still not able to do team reps," Monken said Friday, via NFL.com.

Line up their numbers next to each other and the stakes come into focus. Watson has completed 65.5% of his passes for 1,806 yards, seven touchdown passes and three interceptions in eight starts for a 5-3 team. Sanders threw the same seven touchdown passes in his seven rookie starts, but with 10 interceptions on 56.6% passing in a 3-4 stretch.

Brisker will pay his $17,911. Sanders now gets a Superdome stage to show the Browns' 5-3 start doesn't hinge on one quarterback's health.
