Not only did Uwazurike learn he was going on injured reserve with a shoulder injury, but he also learned the NFL was fining him for his actions in a Week 8 win over the Kansas City Chiefs.

“The Broncos placed DL Eyioma Uwazurike (shoulder) on IR,” The Athletic’s Nick Kosmider wrote on X.

Uwazurike, 6-foot-6 and 320 pounds, was also fined $6,366 by the NFL’s Gameday Accountability Committee for a facemask against the Kansas City Chiefs in Denver’s Week 8 victory.

Uwazurike Becomes Surprise Starter for Broncos

After playing all 17 games in 2025 with just one start, Uwazurike has become a surprise starter for the Broncos in 2026 with seven starts in eight games.

ESPN’s Bill Barnwell projected Uwazurike as one of the NFL’s top backups in 2026.

“Uwazurike’s role will expand after the departure of John Franklin-Myers, but the former fourth-round pick was another unheralded defensive tackle who had his best year as a pro in 2025, generating 3.5 sacks across a career-high 409 snaps,” Barnwell wrote on July 21. “While he’s already 28, Uwazurike’s best football could still be ahead.”

Uwazurike Seemed Poised for Breakout Season

ESPN’s Ben Solak singled out Uwazurike as Denver’s top “breakout candidate” as he continues to repair his reputation following a year-long gambling suspension in 2023.

Uwazurike has been the answer for the Broncos as they try to replace John Franklin-Myers, who left for a 3-year, $63 million free-agent contract with the Tennessee Titans.

text:
Aaron Glenn and the New York Jets can take some solace after the NFL stepped in over the hit on Garrett Wilson in Week 8 against the Las Vegas Raiders that may have led to the receiver's concussion, which will sideline him for Week 9 against the Kansas City Chiefs.

Per the NFL on November 7, Raiders defensive back Jeremy Chinn received a $17,911 fine for "unnecessary roughness."

More specifically, and as expected, the fine was for a "hit on a defenseless player."

During the fourth quarter of the Jets' loss ot the Raiders on a second-and-10 play from New York's 35-yard line Geno Smith found Wilson for 15 yards. Chinn made the tackle, bringing the play to an end.

Officials flagged Chinn for the infraction during the game, making the fine unsurprising even with the NFL's inconsistent history on levying them.

The NFL fined Chinn the standard amount for a first-time infraction of this kind.

Another such incident could incur a fine as high as $23,882, according the league. Chinn can appeal this fine, and he can get some of the money back after the season if he avoids further incident. However, he faces long-term implications, too.

He now has one strike toward a one-game suspension. Two more will trigger the suspension, assuming this decision sticks.

Moreover, Chinn's strike will carry over into future seasons.

Jets Get Bad News as NFL Docks Raiders' Jeremy Chinn Over Garrett Wilson Hit

That the NFL took further action over the hit on Garrett is good. However, the Jets did not emerge from this unscathed.

The NFL also announced that it fined Jets starting right guard Joe Tippman $12,537 for "unncessary roughness" over an illegal "low block" that occurred during the first quarter of thee contest on a first-and-10 run play from the Raiders 34-yard line.

Running back Braelon Allen gained 15 yards on the play, and officials did not throw any flags.

The good news for both the Jets and the Raiders is that there were no other fines levied as a result of this contest.

The NFL levied 31 fines in Week 8, which was the second most in a single week this season. Among the most notable punishments were those handed down to Pittsburgh Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker, Dallas Cowboys linebacker DeMarvion Overshown and Las Vegas Raiders safety Jeremy Chinn. Each fine was the result of a hit that led to the offensive player being placed in concussion protocol and ruled out for Week 9.

Brisker owes the NFL $17,911 for a blow to the head/neck on Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson. The play occurred less than a minute and a half into the Steelers' victory and drew a roughing the passer penalty, which Brisker voiced extreme displeasure with after the game.

"Babying the quarterback," Brisker said. "He's laying there crying, whatever he was doing. It is what it is. I assume I'm going to get fined because if you watch it, I'm hitting him with my chest and them I'm off to the side. But he had his binky today, so they threw it out there. It is what it is."

Watson briefly left the game, and Shedeur Sanders replaced him. The latter threw two passes before Watson returned to action and finished the game. Although Watson practiced in the days leading up to this Sunday's matchup against the New Orleans Saints and cleared the concussion protocol on Saturday, the Browns announced they will turn to Sanders as their Week 9 starter.

Overshown's fine is for his use of his helmet on a hit against Arizona Cardinals running back Bam Knight. He must pay $9,528. The hit jarred the ball loose from Knight's hands, and the Cowboys recovered the fumble without a penalty. The NFL reviewed the play in the wake of the game, however, and issued the fine.

Knight will not play in the Cardinals' divisional clash with the Seattle Seahawks. He did not practice this week.

Chinn sealed a Raiders win last week with an interception in the end zone, but just one play prior, he made forcible contact with New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson on a catch along the sideline, which resulted in a fine. Chinn owes $17,911 for a hit on a defenseless player. The two players' helmets collided on the play, and while Wilson stayed in the game for the Jets' final snap, he later entered concussion protocol.

Wilson reported concussion symptoms the next day, and by midweek the Jets placed him in the protocol. They eventually ruled him out for this week's battle with the Kansas City Chiefs.

There have been 223 plays this season which resulted in a fine. That is 0.0113% of all plays through eight weeks. The 31 fines from Week 8 were second only to the 38 in Week 2.

text:
The Detroit Lions on Saturday, Nov. 7, placed linebacker Jack Campbell on injured reserve.

Campbell (neck) was placed on a backboard and carted off the field in the fourth quarter of Detroit's 19-15 win over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 1. Campbell, who was transported to Henry Ford Hospital, said in a statement through the team Tuesday he has "full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body."

An official diagnosis for Campbell, 26, or a timeline for his recovery have not yet been publicly shared. In his statement, Campbell asked fans to continue praying for him and his family. "We feel the love, and I can’t thank everyone enough," Campbell said.

On Friday, Lions head coach Dan Campbell said Jack Campbell "continues to improve."

"This is about, man, how would he prepare, how would he play?" Dan Campbell said. "Those are the standards for us going into this (next) game. We owe it to him."

Linebackers Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez and Trevor Nowaske are all expected to take on larger roles on defense. Other linebackers on the active roster include Joe Bachie, Amen Ogbongbemiga and K.J. Britt, the latter of whom was signed Wednesday from the New England Patriots' practice squad.

The Lions on Saturday also signed cornerback Nick Whiteside to the active roster and temporarily elevated two players from their practice squad for Sunday's matchup with the Miami Dolphins, in defensive end Anthony Lucas and running back Jabari Small. Lucas earned a shoutout from Dan Campbell during the head coach's news conference Friday, when Campbell said the undrafted rookie from USC has been "somebody we've been repping a little bit here."

Starting defensive end D.J. Wonnum (concussion) won't play against the Dolphins. Neither will center Cade Mays (ankle), cornerback D.J. Reed or safety Kerby Joseph (knee). Juice Scruggs will replace Mays at center, and a combination of players could fill in for Reed at cornerback; options on the outside (in addition to Whiteside) include Roger McCreary, Rock Ya-Sin, Khalil Dorsey and Ennis Rakestraw Jr.

At the defensive end spot opposite of Aidan Hutchinson, Lucas, Derrick Moore and Eric O'Neill are all likely to see increased snaps. Moore has seen at least 20 reps on defense in each of his last three games. He has five pressures on the season thus far, including two quarterback hits.

Colts rookie strong safety A.J.
Haulcy will miss Sunday's game against the Cowboys due to an ankle injury.

text:
Colts rookie strong safety A.J. Haulcy will miss Sunday's game against the Cowboys due to an ankle injury.

Second-year safety Hunter Wohler is expected to start in Haulcy's place.

Haulcy, a third-round pick, has struggled in his first season, allowing three touchdowns in coverage.

Indianapolis has also elevated safeties Trey Washington and Johnathan Edwards from the practice squad due to other injuries in the secondary.

INDIANAPOLIS — The Colts will not have rookie strong safety A.J. Haulcy on Sunday against the Cowboys.

Haulcy suffered an ankle injury in Friday’s practice, and although Indianapolis initially listed the rookie as questionable for Sunday’s game, the Colts downgraded Haulcy to out on Saturday afternoon.

Second-year safety Hunter Wohler presumably steps into the lineup in place of Haulcy on Sunday. Indianapolis also elevated second-year safety Trey Washington from the practice squad.

Haulcy’s injury robs the defense of a starter, although the third-round pick out of LSU has struggled this season, making it unlikely that his absence will be crippling.

Indianapolis has given Haulcy eight starts and 396 snaps, and the rookie has responded with 39 tackles.

But Haulcy has often struggled with the adjustment to the NFL, making mistakes in coverage. Haulcy has allowed three touchdown passes and an opposing quarterback rating of 114.4 when he’s the nearest defender in coverage, according to the NFL’s Next Gen Stats. A ballhawk in college who was known for taking the ball away, Haulcy has only two pass breakups so far.

Wohler, a player the Colts defensive staff has liked the last two years, has 16 tackles in 83 defensive snaps. He has not been targeted much in coverage, according to Next Gen Stats; Wohler has been the nearest defender in coverage on only three snaps so far.

Haulcy’s injury leaves the Colts a little thin in the middle of the defense.

Indianapolis had already declared out the team’s starting slot cornerback, Justin Walley, and the team’s starting middle linebacker, Akeem Davis-Gaither, although Davis-Gaither is not a strong defender in coverage. With Walley out again and Cam Taylor-Britt on injured reserve, the Colts elevated Johnathan Edwards from the practice squad for the second consecutive week.

Facing off against an explosive, talented Cowboys offense, the Colts need a few players to step up in the middle of the defense.

text:
For once this season, it is good news on the injury front for the Rams.

Los Angeles has activated pass rusher Myles Garrett (knee) from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's game against the Commanders, setting up the reigning Defensive Player of the Year to return to the lineup for the first time since Week 1.

Garrett carries no designation into the matchup, and Rams coach Sean McVay told reporters Friday that he is expected to play versus Washington, barring any setbacks.

“Glad to be back on the field with my teammates," Garrett said Friday. "Making an impact, feeling their presence and just integrating back with them again.”

Garrett, who helped make the Rams the story of the offseason thanks to his blockbuster trade from the Browns to L.A., has been unable to make his usual impact on the regular season with the campaign already in November.

Following the team's season-opening loss to the 49ers, during which Garrett logged five pressures but failed to add a sack, tackle or anything else to the stat sheet, the five-time All-Pro underwent knee surgery and was placed on IR.

He missed the past seven contests before being designated to return, practicing in limited fashion twice and taking a rest day Friday. Now, he's officially back.

Garrett rejoins a Rams squad that has far underperformed expectations.

Billed as a superteam after Aaron Donald unretired to join forces with Garrett and other additions such as cornerbacks Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson on a defense that suddenly appeared every bit as good as an offense that led the league in points and yards in 2025, the Rams are 4-4, sitting in third place in the NFC West at the midway point of the season.

They have dealt with myriad injuries beyond Garrett. Star wide receiver Puka Nacua has missed two games and his counterpart Davante Adams is on IR -- as are other big names such as Kobie Turner and Poona Ford. Watson, one of L.A.'s aforementioned additions alongside Garrett, suffered a season-ending shoulder injury last week and on Saturday was placed on IR.

Despite the disappointment thus far, the Rams still rank 10th in points scored and 12th in points allowed, and they're top five in yards both offensively and defensively. Los Angeles' defense also ranks third in quarterback pressure percentage (41.0), though it has resulted in only 12 sacks, which sits tied for 26th.

Outside of the sacks, those are all good, respectable numbers, but Garrett was expected to help elevate the Rams to an otherworldly level.

On the active roster again with a clean bill of health, he can restart his pursuit of that aim, which hardly got started in one injury-affected outing before surgery.

“I think the offenses really have to pick their poison," Garrett said ahead of playing his first NFL game with Donald, who was inactive for the season opener. "Who is going to be freed up this play? I think either of us are pretty good at winning one-on-ones, so we’ll have some fun.”

Garrett, Donald and the Rams kick off against the Commanders at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday.

text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are awaiting the return of several key contributors from the reserve/injured list as they enter the second half of their schedule.

Currently sitting at 6-2 while holding sole possession of first place in the AFC North during their Week 9 bye, the Steelers are in an overall good position. They could upgrade their roster even further by making an addition or two via trade ahead of the November 10 trade deadline, though getting back some of their injured players in the near future should help out a ton as well.

With that, here is every player on IR as well as the reserve/PUP list for Pittsburgh and when they may make their way back onto the field.

DT Derrick Harmon

Harmon was placed on IR with a foot injury he suffered during the first half of Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss to the Cleveland Browns on Thursday Night Football.

Since he's missed the minimum of four games while residing on IR, the 2025 first-round pick is eligible to be activated next week ahead of the Steelers' Week 10 matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football.

Harmon hadn't been working with Pittsburgh's rehab group before its Week 8 rematch with Cleveland. Whether or not his 21-day practice window is opened and/or he returns to the 53-man roster by next week remains to be seen.

WR Michael Pittman Jr.

Pittman Jr. was first ruled out for the Steelers' Week 2 game against the New England Patriots with a foot injury before later being placed on IR, before having a chance to face his old team, the Indianapolis Colts, in Week 5.

The veteran wide receiver spoke with reporters at the start of the bye week on November 2 and stated that he's been doing "a slow progression," which has been "going well."

Pittman Jr. stated that his injury, which started out as plantar fasciitis, has "morphed into something else," which is a bit worrying.

He did state that it would "be great to be back after the bye week," and he can be activated next week since he's already missed four games, but it seems possible that he'll remain on IR beyond that timeframe.

WR Roman Wilson

Wilson suffered a finger injury at the end of the first half vs. Indianapolis in Week 5, resulting in a trip to IR before Pittsburgh's Week 6 bout with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

The third-year receiver has been seen working with the rehab group off to the side during recent practices. Wilson's 21-day practice window has yet to be opened, though that could potentially occur in the near future, and he will be eligible for activation in Week 11.

DT Sebastian Joseph-Day

Joseph-Day was placed on IR before the Steelers' Week 7 game against the New Orleans Saints in Paris with a triceps injury.

In an appearance on 102.5 WDVE earlier this week, Jack Sawyer stated that, "It sucks we're not gonna be able to get Sebastian back for- maybe at all," which painted a worrying picture about the odds of Joseph-Day returning in 2026.

The 31-year-old also isn't eligible to be activated until Week 12 at the earliest if he does progress quicker than expected.

OL Gennings Dunker

A third-round pick out of Iowa in the 2026 NFL Draft, Dunker was placed on IR ahead of Pittsburgh's Week 3 contest vs. the Cincinnati Bengals with an MCL sprain.

The initial timeline for his recovery sat around the four-to-six-week mark, and he's now near the end of that interval.

Dunker became eligible to be activated in Week 7, meaning he can rejoin the 53-man roster at any time once he's cleared.

OL Jack Driscoll

The Steelers put Driscoll on IR with a return designation at final roster cuts in late August due to an undisclosed injury.

The 29-year-old has been eligible to return since Week 5, though there's been just about zero updates on his status throughout the season up to this point.

DL Logan Lee

Lee, who missed his entire rookie season in 2024 due to a calf injury, landed on IR back in August during training camp.

The former sixth-round pick will miss the remainder of the campaign as a result and will look to make his return in 2027 as he enters the final year of his rookie contract.

DB Donte Kent

Kent did not play as a rookie last season after first suffering an ankle injury in training camp and landing on IR before tearing his ACL after his 21-day practice window was opened in early December.

The former seventh-round pick was placed on the active/PUP list at the beginning of training camp this year and was then moved to the reserve/PUP list at the roster cutdown deadline.

Kent has been eligible for activation since Week 5, but his timeline for a possible return in 2026 is unknown at the moment.

text:
New Orleans Saints rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson and left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. have been activated from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns.

Tyson, the eighth overall pick in the 2026 draft, is set to make his NFL debut after injuring his hamstring in August. He returned to practice for the first time since injuring his right hamstring in a joint practice against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Aug. 13.

He has been listed as questionable on the injury report along with Banks, who also returned to practice following surgery on his ankle.

Tyson was expected to be out at least two months after the hamstring injury, which occurred after he landed awkwardly after catching a pass. Both Tyson and the Saints said the injury was not related to his previous hamstring issues from college; he missed three games for Arizona State last year.

He also tore his ACL, MCL and PCL in his left knee when he was at Colorado in 2022, fractured his collarbone in 2024 and sprained his ankle that caused him to miss spring practices in 2025.

Tyson said he feels like the extended time to get himself right has been "a blessing."

"Kind of got a slow start to the NFL, so I got to kind of take my time and kind of really adjust to it," he said.

The Saints released running back Kendre Miller as a corresponding move.

Miller, a 2023 third-round pick out of TCU, led the Saints' struggling run game with 159 yards this season. The Saints released him after claiming running back Audric Estime off waivers from the Cleveland Browns. Estime was with the team last year and in camp but was waived with an injury settlement.

text:
Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell's road to recovery is on the hearts and minds of teammates, coaches and fans as the Lions prepare for their Week 9 road game against the Miami Dolphins.

Campbell and the Lions have provided progressively positive updates after the linebacker was carted off the field on Sunday, Nov. 1, when he fell limp to the Ford Field turf after tackling Minnesota Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson.

Campbell has been hospitalized at Henry Ford Hospital in Detroit since suffering an undisclosed spinal injury. While much remains publicly unknown about Campbell's diagnosis, recovery and long-term prognosis, here's what we know as the Lions (5-2) prepare for what's sure to be an emotional game against the 1-6 Dolphins.

What's the latest Jack Campbell injury update?

Campbell posted his first, and so far only, public statement following his injury on Wednesday, Nov. 4, announcing that he has full movement in his lower body and was continuing to make progress with movement in his upper body. It marked the first concrete update on the linebacker's condition since he suffered a neck injury during the Lions' Week 8 victory over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 1.

Prior to his statement, the updates had been more general and left many concerned about Campbell's condition after he was carted off the field on a backboard.

"I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic," Campbell wrote. "I'm taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better."

Is Jack Campbell still in the hospital?

The Lions have not provided updates about where Campbell is receiving treatment beyond saying that he was hospitalized following the injury, and Campbell on Wednesday, Nov. 4, thanking his caregivers at Henry Ford Hospital in Detroit and the Detroit Lions medical staff.

Is Jack Campbell paralyzed?

Campbell appears to have avoided the worst fears that immediately followed his injury, as his updates indicate that he has avoided full paralysis from the neck down. Campbell said he has "full movement in my lower body" and was working to regain upper-body movement as part of his recovery.

Does Jack Campbell have central cord syndrome?

Campbell's medical diagnosis has not yet been made public. Medical experts reached by USA TODAY did point out the uniqueness of Campbell's post-injury symptoms, saying that delayed recovery of upper-body movement could be associated with central cord syndrome. It's a rare medical condition common in people with spinal injuries who have fallen forward and land on their forehead and extend backward, similar to the action exhibited by Campbell’s head and neck at impact.

“I think it’s great news (if it’s central cord syndrome) because it’s an incomplete spinal-cord injury,” neurosurgeon Dr. Betsy Grunch said, “and if he’s already recovering as quickly as reported, then it’s quite possible he can make a full recovery.”

Is Jack Campbell out for the season? Will he play again?

The Lions have not provided any timeline for Campbell to return to football activities, as he likely faces an extended period of recovery and rest as he works toward regaining full function of his extremities.

Campbell, in his statement, said: "My faith in God has never been stronger. I know He has a plan for me, and I trust in that plan. I know there may be challenges ahead, but with my faith, my family, and so many people in my corner, I know we’ll get through this."

When do the Lions play the Dolphins in Week 9?

The Lions will play their first game without Campbell against the Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens. Kickoff is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET on Sunday, Nov. 8.

What Lions coaches said about Jack Campbell

“We’re going to prepare like he prepared,” Lions assistant head coach Scottie Montgomery said this week. “We’re going to play like he plays. We’re going to do the things that he would have us to do.”

Dan Campbell stressed the importance of refocusing on the game ahead.

“Jack continues to improve, which is all great news, and again this is about, man, how would he prepare, how would he play?” the Lions head coach said. “Those are the standards for us going into this game. We owe it to him.”

What teammates said about Jack Campbell

Campbell is a team captain for the Lions, so it's no surprise his teammates have spoken highly of him before and after the injury.

Campbell's fellow defensive star Aidan Hutchinson had high praise for the team captain after last week's game.

"He's everything, man," he said. "He's captain, leader, teammate, husband, father, everything. So yeah, we're all praying for him."

text:
A concerning update about Deshaun Watson emerged on Friday. It came amid the Cleveland Browns' announcement that Shedeur Sanders will start for them in Week 9 against the New Orleans Saints.

Watson suffered a concussion last Sunday during Cleveland's 27-6 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. The league takes these cases seriously and players need to pass a series of tests before they are cleared to return to action. The star quarterback has appeared and started in the first eight games of the season. He has 163-of-249 completions for 1,806 yards and seven touchdowns against three interceptions.

Watson joined the Browns in March 2022 following a trade from the Houston Texans. He then signed a fully guaranteed, five-year, $230 million deal, making it the largest guaranteed contract in NFL history at the time. The former Clemson star entered the league in 2017 as the No. 17 overall pick.

Worrying Deshaun Watson News Emerges on Friday

Deshaun Watson returned to practice on Friday but remains in concussion protocol. He missed the sessions in the previous two games, with Sanders taking first team reps. The second-year quarterback has been named the QB1 for Sunday. ESPN's Adam Schefter issued an update on Watson's condition.

"Deshaun Watson was checked for a concussion during the game, cleared the NFL's concussion protocol during the game, and then shortly after the game reported symptoms to the team," Schefter said. "And at that point, they knew he would end up in the concussion protocol. So (he) did not practice Wednesday and Thursday (but) was able to practice today.

"(He) has not cleared the protocol, but there is at least a chance they could be active as a backup. And the reason why he's not starting is because generally starting quarterbacks need reps to go out and play effectively."

The Browns saw their two-game winning streak snapped by the Steelers. However, they still have a winning record and have a chance to improve to 6-3 with a Week 9 victory and Sanders under center.

NFL Week 9 Injury Report: Quarterbacks Lamar Jackson, Baltimore Ravens Jackson lasted one offensive play before suffering an injury to the thumb on his throwing hand.

text:
I’ll say it, the injury bug was not kind this weekend. Many players left the game due to injury at various points, and while some were able to return, others faced what could be season-ending injuries. Luckily for fantasy football managers, only the Pittsburgh Steelers and Tennessee Titans are on bye this week, which increases the number of options to replace these injured players.

NFL Week 9 Injury Report: Quarterbacks

Lamar Jackson, Baltimore Ravens

Jackson lasted one offensive play before suffering an injury to the thumb on his throwing hand. As a result of this injury, he will be placed on IR and will potentially miss the rest of this season. With Tyler Huntley also leaving the game with a turf toe injury, the Ravens turned to Joe Fagnano for the remainder of the game, who also left the game less than 100 percent after taking a hit to the knee.

Kyler Murray, Minnesota Vikings

Murray is dealing with a hamstring strain that hampered him in the game last week. He’s currently not expected to play, which means Carson Wentz will get the start against the Bills.

Deshaun Watson, Cleveland Browns

Watson is dealing with a concussion and related symptoms, and he is unlikely to start this weekend per Ian Rapoport. Shaduer Sanders is expected to start in his place.

Sam Darnold, Seattle Seahawks

Darnold is dealing with a quadriceps injury and has officially been ruled out against the Cardinals. Drew Lock has been limited at practice as he deals with elbow soreness in his throwing arm, which may mean we see either a heavier dose of the rushing attack or Jalen Milroe.

NFL Week 9 Injury Report: Running Backs

Jeremiyah Love, Arizona Cardinals

Love reinjured his ankle in the second quarter against the Cowboys, and as a result, was ruled out for the remainder of the game. With Zonovan Knight suffering a concussion, the Cardinals turned to Tyler Allgeier, who turned in a career performance and is expected to be the main focal point of the rushing attack.

Cam Skattebo, New York Giants

Skattebo is dealing with a hamstring injury, and at this time it seems unlikely that he will play Sunday against the Eagles as he enters the weekend with a doubtful tag. With Tyrone Tracy on injured reserve, it seems most likely that Devin Singletary will get the start, with Greg Desrosiers Jr. as the next man up.

David Montgomery, Houston Texans

Head coach DeMeco Ryans stated this week that Montgomery is still week-to-week but did state that he has made some progress. That said, he will be out this Sunday against the Chargers. Woody Marks gets the nod yet again.

Kyle Monangai, Chicago Bears

Monangai returned to practice Friday in a limited fashion. As a result, he’s being listed as questionable. I would not get my hopes up, and as a Bears fan I’m not, but ideally he can return to action this week.

Brian Robinson, Atlanta Falcons

Robinson Jr. has been ruled out yet again as he continues to deal with a hamstring injury. Expect another serious workload for Bijan Robinson.

Breece Hall, New York Jets

Hall is considered good to go and is expected to return to action next Sunday against the Chiefs. Braelon Allen has been a star while replacing Hall, so we could see a snap split on both players, making them both less than ideal fantasy options.

TreVeyon Henderson, New England Patriots

Henderson made a statement Friday that he’s dealing with an unusual medical situation that includes unexplained neurological symptoms. He is not expected to play at this time, and may be away from action until this is resolved. Rhamondre Stevenson should see a bump in snap count.

NFL Week 9 Injury Report: Wide Receivers

Garrett Wilson, New York Jets

Wilson suffered a concussion last week. He has not cleared protocol at this time and will be out this Sunday against the Chiefs. Adonai Mitchell becomes an interesting flex option as a result.

Michael Wilson, Arizona Cardinals

Wilson suffered multiple broken ribs during the 33-30 win over the Cowboys on Sunday. It remains to be seen if he will miss any time, so practice reports this week will be crucial for us to follow.

Christian Watson, Green Bay Packers

Watson has been limited at practice as he manages a broken rib, but all signs currently point to him being active this weekend. If he is unable to go, the rest of the pass-catching room will have to step up, as Watson is a crucial part of this passing attack.

Jordan Tyson, New Orleans Saints

Tyson is expected to be reinstated from the injured reserve as early as this week, and could even make his debut this coming weekend. This would be a bump for the Saints offense that lacks true receiving options past Chris Olave.

George Pickens, Dallas Cowboys

Pickens will be limited Friday as he deals with a hamstring injury. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer is hopeful that Pickens will be good to go this weekend, but there is a chance he will not be able to play.

Emeka Egbuka, Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Egbuka returned to practice this week in a limited fashion. That said, he is being listed as questionable this weekend, and ultimately we won’t know his status fully until then.

A.J. Brown, New England Patriots

Brown is dealing with both knee and ankle injuries, which is keeping him out of practice. He will be inactive this weekend.

DeVonta Smith, Philadelphia Eagles

Smith continues to miss practice with a hamstring injury. He’s being listed as out this week, and with Dontayvion Wicks also inactive, the passing attack will take a hit yet again.

Mike Evans, San Francisco 49ers

Evans has not practiced as he continues to deal with Achilles tendonitis and has been ruled out. With Deebo Samuel also not practicing, and Christian Kirk also out, it currently seems like Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks, and Jacob Cowing will be the receiving options for Brock Purdy.

NFL Week 9 Injury Report: Tight Ends

Jake Ferguson, Dallas Cowboys

Ferguson is returning to practice on Friday, which shows he is making progress and could return to action this weekend. This would be a bump for the Cowboys offense, which will need to continue to attempt to carry this roster.

Terrance Ferguson, Los Angeles Rams

Ferguson has been limited in practice as he is attempting to return from the Injured Reserve for an ankle injury, but also picked up a hamstring issue during practice Friday. With Colby Parkinson also sidelined with a rib injury, Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen will likely see the majority of work at TE yet again.

text:
New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown will miss his second consecutive game due to a knee injury that has hampered him throughout his career, but the team isn't down on his prospects, insider Tom Pelissero reported on Saturday.

The Patriots traded a 2028 first-round pick to acquire Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles this offseason, but the results have been underwhelming through the first half of the season. Brown suffered an ankle injury during the team's regular-season opener against the Seattle Seahawks.

The 29-year-old returned from a stint on the injured reserve list in Week 6, and he played four days later when the Patriots faced the Chicago Bears on Thursday Night Football. Then, Brown popped up on the injury report with a knee issue.

The quick turnaround between the games may have put additional stress on Brown's knee, but the Patriots are "optimistic" he could return after the team's Week 11 bye, according to Pelissero.

The Los Angeles Rams were also interested in trading for Brown during the offseason, but they were reportedly scared off by the medical concerns with his knee, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported. New England head coach Mike Vrabel, who drafted Brown during his time as head coach of the Tennessee Titans, was evidently more comfortable with the medical evaluations.

Brown has only caught passes in each of the three games he played in this season, bringing his tally up to nine receptions for 101 yards and no touchdowns. There was belief that the eight-year veteran would be a great fit as a vertical threat for quarterback Drake Maye, who has been one of the best deep-ball passers in the league. That hasn't proven to be the case: Brown is only averaging 8.3 yards per catch — significantly down from his career average of 15.3 yards per reception.

text:
The New England Patriots could enter Sunday's game against the Green Bay Packers without one of the most dependable pieces of Drake Maye's passing attack.

Tight end Hunter Henry is questionable with a foot injury after missing Wednesday and Thursday practices. Henry returned in a limited capacity Friday, providing some encouragement, but his availability remains uncertain heading into the weekend.

The situation carries an interesting distinction. According to the Patriots, Maye has never played an entire game in his NFL career without Henry available, making a potential absence against Green Bay an unfamiliar challenge for the quarterback.

Henry Has Been Maye's Reliable Option

Henry leads New England with 29 receptions through eight games and ranks second on the team with 326 receiving yards. His production reflects a role that extends beyond simply serving as another pass catcher in the offense.

The veteran has provided Maye with a dependable target over the middle, particularly when defenses make it difficult to generate longer completions. His experience also matters in situations where the quarterback must identify coverage and make quick decisions before pressure arrives.

Henry suffered the injury during last Sunday's victory over Miami, leaving the game in the second quarter after playing only eight offensive snaps. The Patriots nevertheless escaped with a 24-19 victory, but facing Green Bay without him would create a different challenge against a defense capable of disrupting passing plays.

New England's Depth Could Be Tested

The Patriots already know A.J. Brown will miss Sunday's game because of ankle and knee issues. Mack Hollins is also questionable while working toward a possible return from injured reserve, increasing the importance of New England's remaining healthy receivers and tight ends.

Maye has shown an ability to generate explosive plays this season, but those opportunities become more difficult when an offense loses multiple established targets. Green Bay can devote additional attention to the remaining receiving options if Henry is unavailable.

The Packers also have recorded 22 sacks through eight games, making reliable protection and quick passing decisions important parts of New England's offensive preparation.

Friday Offered Some Encouragement

Henry's return to practice was a positive development after two consecutive absences. However, limited participation does not guarantee that he will be ready for a full workload Sunday.

The Patriots will continue evaluating his condition before making a final game-day decision. If Henry can play, his presence would give Maye a familiar option in a difficult game.

text:
SANTA CLARA — Brandon Aiyuk pulled up 13 minutes early Friday afternoon for a meeting he and his agent had scheduled with 49ers representatives.

Aiyuk, who sustained a severe knee injury on Oct. 20, 2024, declared himself healthy enough to resume his NFL career.

That part remains very much undetermined as Aiyuk entered the 49ers’ business office along Great America Parkway.

“Nice to see y’all,” Aiyuk said to a couple dozen reporters stationed outside the team offices. “I’m feeling great, feeling healthy. It was a long recovery process, a long rehab process, but I’m back to 100 percent and looking to get reinstated into the National Football League.”

The 49ers placed Aiyuk on the reserve/left squad list in December. In July 2025, the 49ers voided $27 million in guaranteed money for his failure to adhere to the terms of his contract.

Recently, Aiyuk hired agent Drew Rosenhaus to assist in the process of getting reinstated into the NFL.

“Obviously, Brandon is here to meet with the team,” Rosenhaus said. “Fortunately, he’s feeling good physically. He’s healthy. He’s ready to get back to work.

Aiyuk signed a four-year, $120 million contract extension with the 49ers before the start of the 2024 regular season. He received a $23 million signing bonus. San Francisco is seeking approximately $13 million in bonus forfeiture, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reported Thursday.

Ben Johnson's offense is operating well below its peak, at least on the ground. Although running back D'Andre Swift has six rushing touchdowns during the current winning streak, he averaged less than 3.0 yards per carry twice in the same span. Few veteran RBs can carry a backfield against physical defenses for an extend period of time. Fortunately, help is coming.

Kyle Monangai returned to practice in limited fashion on Friday, making him questionable for Sunday night's prime-time collision with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, per The 33rd Team's Ari Meirov. The 2025 seventh-round draft pick has not played since Oct. 4 due to toe and thumb injuries.

Even if Monangai cannot take the field in Week 9, it is deeply encouraging to see him clear this roadblock. The 5-foot-8, 207-pounder boasts 324 rushing yards and three TDs in four games played, averaging an excellent 5.4 yards per attempt.

The Bears (6-2) lead the NFL with 281 rushes and rank second with 150.8 rushing yards per game (Bucs are No. 1). Heavy run volume is a major part of Johnson's game plan, and Swift can only endure so many hits on his own. Simply put, the 24-year-old Kyle Monangai is arguably the biggest X-factor on this offense.

It will be important to see how he responds after the layoff. Those type of injuries can certainly linger throughout the campaign. The Bears still trust D'Andre Swift, though, and do not have to hasten Monangai's return. The Bears go on their bye in Week 10, so there is potential benefit to giving the former Rutgers star a little more time off.

text:
The New England Patriots will face the Green Bay Packers without having to account for one of the NFL's most disruptive defensive players.

Green Bay officially ruled out Micah Parsons for Sunday's game at Gillette Stadium as the star edge rusher continues working toward a return from a serious knee injury. Parsons practiced on a limited basis Friday, but the Packers determined he was not ready to play.

The absence removes a major potential challenge for Drake Maye and New England's offensive line. However, another Green Bay injury could have important consequences on the opposite side of the football.

Parsons Will Have To Wait For Return

Parsons has been recovering from an ACL and meniscus injury suffered last December against Denver. The Packers recently opened his practice window, creating optimism that he could return to action in the coming weeks.

That return will not happen against New England. Green Bay ruled him out Friday, meaning the Patriots will not have to prepare for his explosive pass-rushing ability during Sunday's contest.

The development is significant for an offense already dealing with injuries to several important skill-position players. A.J. Brown has been ruled out, while Hunter Henry remains questionable, increasing the importance of keeping Maye comfortable in the pocket.

Green Bay still has a capable defensive front and entered the week with 22 sacks. New England cannot assume that Parsons' absence will eliminate the Packers' ability to pressure the quarterback.

Green Bay Also Loses Starting Center

The Packers ruled out offensive lineman Sean Rhyan with an ankle injury, creating another potential opening for New England.

Rhyan's absence will force Green Bay to adjust its interior offensive line against a Patriots defense that has been effective against the run. New England enters the contest allowing 92.6 rushing yards per game, ranking sixth in the NFL.

Green Bay has struggled to establish a consistent rushing attack, averaging just 60.6 yards per game through eight contests. Changes along the offensive line could make it even more difficult to create running lanes against New England's defensive front.

The Patriots also recorded five sacks in last Sunday's victory over Miami, demonstrating their ability to generate pressure when opponents face difficult passing situations.

MORE: Patriots' AJ Brown Trade Could Lead to Lack of Deadline Additions

Patriots Must Capitalize On Opportunity

Green Bay has ruled out five players overall, including Parsons, Rhyan, linebacker Zaire Franklin, offensive lineman Travis Glover and tight end Josh Whyle.

The Packers still enter Sunday with a 5-3 record and a productive passing offense, so the Patriots will face a significant challenge regardless of the injuries.

But the absence of Parsons could help New England's passing game, while Rhyan's absence could create opportunities for its defensive front.

Those are meaningful developments in a game between two teams attempting to strengthen their playoff positions. The Patriots now must turn those potential advantages into production on the field.

text:
Before Cleveland Browns coach Todd Monken announced on Aug. 24 that he was naming Deshaun Watson the team's starting quarterback over Shedeur Sanders, he spoke with Sanders in his office about his forward-looking approach.

Ten weeks later, Sanders is poised to make his first start of the 2026 NFL season Sunday at the New Orleans Saints (1 p.m. ET, CBS) as Watson remains sidelined in the NFL's concussion protocol.

"He's very diligent and he likes to play football, has a natural confidence about him," Monken said Friday. "Just like any young player, they've got to play. ... Where he's improved is his footwork, his drops, his mechanics, understanding where to go with the ball, sense of urgency in terms of working through his progressions, protections. There were so many things he needed to work on, and he's done that like any young player. Any young player has a lot to work on, especially at the quarterback position.

"And you can see that from the moment we got here and that's why we opened up the competition and we split the reps was because of his ascent."

Sanders' first start of the season comes at a critical time. The Browns are 5-3 after a Week 8 road loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers that knocked Cleveland out of first place in the AFC North. ESPN Analytics gives the Browns a 16.5% chance of making the playoffs. A win against the Saints would increase their odds to 25.4% ahead of four straight home games.

Sanders made seven starts as a rookie last season and went 3-4 in those games, but he posted a 19.0 Total QBR, the fifth-lowest mark among 696 quarterbacks with at least 200 pass attempts in a season in the QBR era (since 2006). He has spent the first eight weeks of the regular season as the backup, getting minimal practice reps, but he has familiarity with the starting offense after splitting reps with Watson in the quarterback competition during training camp.

"I'm just excited to see him go play and hopefully let it rip, which I think he'll do," Browns offensive coordinator Travis Switzer said this week. "He did it [Wednesday] in practice. Go lead, be in command, which I think he's grown tremendously in that area, really since we got here.

"And I think Monk[en] mentioned this the other day, but when you're going through training camp, and we were splitting, and really all the spring, we were splitting a lot of those reps as we were going through all the installs, and we were able to see him in a lot more reps than probably a typical backup would be, because obviously we were finding out who our quarterback was going to be. So, hopefully he can review back to some of those things if it were to be him, and yeah, let it rip. Play with confidence."

Coaches and teammates have praised Sanders' growth in recent months. In New Orleans, he will get the opportunity to display that progression and lead a struggling offense that ranks 29th in points per game (17.4).

Here are the three ways Shedeur Sanders can showcase his progress:

Playing within structure

The tendency for Sanders to hold on to the ball has been a talking point since his time at Colorado. Sanders has acknowledged he tends to hold the ball in efforts to make a big play -- sometimes to his own detriment. As a rookie, Sanders averaged 3.24 seconds to throw, the slowest among 38 quarterbacks who made at least six starts in 2025.

In August, Monken highlighted Sanders' growth in striking a balance between playing within structure and also making plays by holding on to the ball.

"Being able to check the ball down and get it out of his hands; he's such a playmaker that that's hard for him," Monken said. "For a guy that is always looking to make a play, super competitive, that is a win. Trying to get super competitive quarterbacks to understand that throwing the ball away and eliminating lost yardage plays is a win."

In 25 dropbacks across two games in the preseason, Sanders had an average time to throw of 3.10 seconds, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. The Browns have the fifth-most yards after catch in the NFL (1,019) this season.

Getting the ball to pass catchers in the flow of the offense plays a big role in that. It also helps to prevent sacks. Watson has taken the most sacks in the league (33), in part because he has held the ball for too long at times.

Taking care of the ball

Sanders threw 10 interceptions from Weeks 11 to 18 last season, which led all quarterbacks in the league during that time frame. Not every pick was the result of a bad decision or throw; some were caused by dropped passes or batted balls.

But at times, Sanders played a risky brand of football that lent itself to turnovers. He had four dropped interceptions from Weeks 11 to 18, twice as many as the next-closest quarterback during that same time span, according to ESPN Research, and tied for the most by any player all of last season.

This season, Watson has only thrown three interceptions, but he has seven fumbles, which leads all quarterbacks, and has lost three fumbles.

Pre-snap operation

A major point of emphasis for Monken during the quarterback competition was the pre-snap operation. Monken heaps plenty of responsibility on his QBs to get the offense in and out of the huddle properly, make the correct adjustments at the line of scrimmage, use cadence correctly and limit pre-snap penalties.

The latter has been an issue for Cleveland through eight games. According to ESPN Research, the Browns have five delay of game penalties, tied for the fifth most in the league, as well as five illegal formation penalties, which are tied for the fourth most. Not all of those infractions fall on the quarterback, but it is largely their responsibility to take control of the pre-snap operation and "eliminate anxiety," in the words of Monken.

When asked to assess Sanders' brief three plays against Pittsburgh while Watson was checked for a concussion, Monken alluded to "a couple plays he could have helped us out with a check" but added that it was unfair to grade Sanders with such limited practice reps.

A raucous environment at the Caesars Superdome will provide a tough test for Sanders, but coaches have said they don't anticipate needing to adjust the game plan or pre-snap operation with Sanders under center.

"The more anxiety that we can relieve pre-snap, which usually comes down to the play clock, just having as much time as possible before the play clock to allow us to operate and relieve that anxiety, I think that's going to be huge," Switzer said.

"As far as the snap count goes, when we're in the gun we'll be in silent [count], and we've been in silent every road game this year. So that part I don't think is really a whole lot different, but certainly just trying to put a premium, like we always do, but especially this week with them being indoors and it being a loud place, we talk about the four twos. Our pre-snap, in and out of the huddle. Shortening calls as a staff as much as we possibly can.

"Monk[en] will talk about getting the play in as fast as possible, which he always tries to do. All those things are certainly at a premium when you play at a place like that," Switzer said.

text:
Jets edge rusher David Bailey will be back after missing the Raiders loss with a groin injury, providing a much-needed boost to the defense which has allowed at least 26 points in each game of their three-game losing streak.

Aaron Glenn said he needs to see “improvement” from the unit, especially in regards to committing penalties on third down.

Bailey will help, they hope, in limiting the Chiefs’ run game — an area Glenn said the rookie has improved “drastically” in, including with his mental approach.

He’s also been solid against the passing game, but the challenge of dealing with Patrick Mahomes figures to be especially tough.

“We already know how good he is at rushing [the QB],’’ Glenn said. “We just have to understand that with Mahomes, he’s gonna fake a throw, he’s gonna move around. We’ve got to make sure we squeeze the pocket and make sure we don’t let him out of the pocket in situations like that.”

Bailey, a full participant in Friday’s practice, said he’s “feeling good” after a “tough” week in which he was forced to sit out against the Raiders.

Now, he’ll be tasked with helping to contain Mahomes — who, like Bailey, played at Texas Tech.

“I’ve never met him formally,’’ Bailey said. “He’s definitely a big name in the league.”

Asked about the key to keeping Mahomes in check, Bailey said, “Just sticking to the game plan [and] sticking to our responsibilities.”

Stop us if you’ve heard this before: No team has fewer interceptions than the Jets this season.

They enter Sunday’s game with just one on the season — Minkah Fitzpatrick’s in Chicago in Week 4.

“It is surprising,’’ Glenn said of his team’s lack of success in that area again. “It’s something that we talk about a lot. But there are other ways to take the ball away and we try to make sure we focus on all aspects of how we take the ball away. [With] punch-outs, guys are doing a really good job of that.”

To Glenn’s point, only the Raiders have forced more fumbles (12) than the Jets (10) on the year and no team has recovered more (seven).

But for a team that stressed the importance of forcing more takeaways, the inability to get more interceptions remains an issue.

“That’s one area we have to improve on, is interceptions,” Glenn said. “It’s something we talk about a lot.”

The Jets are last in the NFL in touchdowns from the red zone at just 42.3 percent. Last week against the Raiders, they were even worse at 2-for-6.

“It’s not enough and we have to be better,’’ offensive coordinator Frank Reich said of the red-zone woes. “We just have to be better. There’s a sense of urgency among players and coaches. From the coaching staff’s perspective, there are two things you do: You scheme it and you coach it. From the players’ perspective, they have to bring it to life. But no matter what, we’re in it together, and collectively as a group, we just have to do better in the red zone.” … CB Nahshon Wright (back) was added to the injury report as questionable. He has yet to play a defensive snap this season after signing a one-year, $3.5 million contract with the team in free agency.

text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Green Bay Packers cornerback Keisean Nixon is questionable for Sunday’s game against the New England Patriots.

Not all questionable designations are created equal, and Nixon’s jovial conversation with reporters after practice on Friday strongly suggests he will be on the field against the defending AFC champions.

“I don’t know, man,” Nixon said. “I hope I wake up Sunday and I feel good enough to play in the game. We’ll see. I hope so.”

Nixon did not practice on Thursday and was limited participation on Friday. Was he taking a rest day on Thursday?

“I just hope I’ll be ready to play on Sunday. We’ll see,” Nixon said. The tone of his voice, however, took all the mystery out of it.

Reporters on Fridays only to get to watch the players go through the opening warmups. Nixon was running around, making leaping catches on balls thrown by Xavier McKinney and typically running around like a fully healthy player.

“I was running? You saw that?” Nixon said.

Yes, and it’s on video.

“That was AI. It was AI. It was not me. I was AI, for sure. For sure, AI,” Nixon said.

What about the smile on the practice field?

“That was AI,” Nixon replied. “Whatever y’all are doing to edit them videos is crazy. Y’all are getting good at it. For sure.”

That Nixon is going to play is no surprise. He hasn’t missed a game since signing with the Packers in 2022.

“Yeah, we always talk about how your best ability is your availability and the fact that he’s been able to do that is pretty uncommon. So, he’s a ‘G,’” coach Matt LaFleur said.

Including playoffs, this would be Nixon’s 81st consecutive game in a Packers uniform.

“It’s not really a streak that means something to me. I just don’t want to not play,” Nixon said. “Technically, I don’t look at it as, ‘Oh, I never missed a game.’ I just want to play every week, so I get my body prepared for it to play. Me just not missing a game is just because I want to play.”

Five Players Out for Packers

Five players are out for the Packers, including edge rusher Micah Parsons, who was designated for return this week following last year’s torn ACL. He was limited participation at all three practices this week, an obvious good sign as he anticipates progressing into team drills next week.

The four other players who are out are starting linebacker and defensive captain Zaire Franklin (shin), starting center Sean Rhyan (ankle), former starting right guard Travis Glover (knee) and tight end Josh Whyle (concussion). Those players missed all three practices this week.

Along with Nixon, running backs Chris Brooks (ankle) and MarShawn Lloyd (knee) are questionable. Brooks was designated for return after missing the last four games; he could be added to the roster on Saturday.

SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- The San Francisco 49ers will welcome defensive end Nick Bosa (calf) and running back Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) back from injury Sunday while receiver Mike Evans will miss his second consecutive game because of Achilles tendinitis.

Bosa, who has been out since before a Week 3 game against Arizona Cardinals, returned to practice this week and participated in some capacity for all three sessions this week. He has no injury designation for Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders and is good to go.

"I feel great," Bosa said. "Bye week was a good extra week for me and I'm ready to go."

Likewise, McCaffrey also does not have an injury designation after suffering a minor hamstring strain in Week 7 against the Atlanta Falcons. McCaffrey did not practice Wednesday but participated on Thursday and Friday on his way to being cleared.

Much like Bosa, McCaffrey said the Week 8 bye helped his recovery so he would not miss any time.

"It wasn't too bad," McCaffrey said. "I think having the bye week was awesome, but I feel great."

Evans, meanwhile, continues to deal with Achilles tendinitis that flared up in a Week 6 win against the Washington Commanders. He did not play against the Falcons and then had the bye week to continue recovering.

Although Evans has made "a lot of progress," according to coach Kyle Shanahan, the Niners don't want to risk pushing him too hard too soon so his injury doesn't get worse.

"I think you learn from the history," general manager John Lynch told KNBR radio in San Francisco on Thursday. "Christian had this situation and every player is different, every situation is different but you don't want it to become something that really lingers. So, we're trying to knock it out such that when he comes back, we give him the best chance to stay back."

In addition to Evans, the Niners ruled out fellow wideouts Deebo Samuel Sr. (hamstring) and Christian Kirk (knee) for Sunday. Kirk injured his meniscus in practice Wednesday. It's unclear whether Kirk will need surgery, Shanahan said.

In better receiver news, Shanahan said it's likely the team will activate Demarcus Robinson (ankle) from injured reserve to play against the Raiders. That would leave a group of Robinson, Jordan Watkins, Jacob Cowing, Brandin Cooks and, likely, KhaDarel Hodge being elevated from the practice squad, as the team's receivers for Sunday.

text:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- The NFL told disgruntled receiver Brandon Aiyuk that he needs to repay the San Francisco 49ers about $13 million he previously received in bonuses as he tries to get reinstated to the team's roster.

Aiyuk's new agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said earlier this week that Aiyuk had officially submitted his paperwork to the NFL to get back and was planning to report to the 49ers on Friday.

A person with knowledge of the situation said the league sent Aiyuk and the NFLPA a letter Thursday saying that he owes the 49ers the money based on bonuses he was paid after signing a four-year, $120 million extension just before the start of the 2024 season. The person spoke on condition of anonymity because the letter was not released.

The Ringer first reported that the Niners were seeking the money back from Aiyuk.

San Francisco general manager John Lynch told the team's flagship radio station KNBR on Thursday that it was a "unique" situation that the team was trying to work through.

"My job is to look out for the best interests of the 49ers, and as such, in this particular situation, we're working with the NFL management council to navigate through kind of a different situation," Lynch said. "It's fluid. I'm going to kind of leave it at that because I've been recommended to do so, and I think it's the right thing to do. We'll look for a pathway for both sides here that works."

MORE: Brandon Aiyuk files to be reinstated, plans to report to 49ers on Friday

Aiyuk hasn't played a game in more than two years since going down with a knee injury in October 2024 and has been on the reserve/left squad list after leaving the Niners late last season.

He fired agent Ryan Williams during his long-running dispute with the 49ers and was without representation until he recently hired Rosenhaus.

Aiyuk will remain under contract with the 49ers after he is reinstated by the NFL. Lynch previously has said he doesn't expect Aiyuk to play for the Niners again, while coach Kyle Shanahan said on Wednesday when asked if Aiyuk could play for San Francisco again that "there are no absolutes in life."

The 49ers previously voided $27 million guaranteed in Aiyuk's contract for 2026 for failing to participate in meetings and other team activities last summer when he was rehabilitating his knee injury.

Aiyuk signed the big extension just before the start of the 2024 season following a lengthy contract hold-in that kept him out of training camp. He was coming off a 2023 season when he had 75 catches for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns and was a second-team All-Pro.

Aiyuk had only 25 catches for 374 yards in seven games in 2024 before getting injured. The 28-year-old has 294 catches for 4,305 yards and 25 TDs since being drafted in the first round in 2020.

text:
RENTON, Wash. -- One week after arriving via a trade, Seattle Seahawks All-Pro left guard Quenton Nelson needs a "minor procedure" on his knee, coach Mike Macdonald said Friday.

Sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport that Nelson's surgery will be to clean out cartilage in his knee.

Macdonald said Nelson will not go on injured reserve, and he'll be designated as week-to-week.

Nelson and quarterback Sam Darnold, who has a quad injury, are among six starters ruled out by the Seahawks (4-4) for Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals (3-5) at Lumen Field. The others are defensive tackle Leonard Williams (stinger), outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu (ankle), left tackle Charles Cross (ankle) and wide receiver/returner Rashid Shaheed (knee).

While Nelson is out, Seattle will move Grey Zabel back to left guard and reinsert Anthony Bradford into the starting lineup at right guard. After acquiring Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick, the Seahawks moved Zabel to right guard, where Bradford had been their starter.

"He had something that he was dealing with when he got here and we re-imaged it and it was aggravated to some degree," Macdonald said of Nelson's injury. "We've kind of done the due diligence, and everybody agrees that it's best to take care of it now and play the long game. He'll be week-to-week at this point."

Nelson, 30, played every offensive snap in the Seahawks' loss to the Chicago Bears on Monday night. He was seen this week with a sleeve on his right leg, was listed as limited Wednesday and did not practice the past two days.

"I can't give you all the details on what it was and what we found," Macdonald said. "Obviously, he passed the physical, so I think two things are true: One, that it was something that he was dealing with coming out of whatever game it was before the trade, and I think it's been aggravated since he got here."

Darnold, who suffered a cracked rib on the second play of Monday's game and then injured his quad toward the end of the game, will not go on IR, Macdonald said.

Macdonald on Friday said Drew Lock will be the starter against the Cardinals, despite a right elbow injury that had him inactive the past two games and limited his throwing in recent weeks. He was again listed as a limited participant Friday, as he has been on all 12 injury reports released since the start of Week 6.

Macdonald said earlier in the week that the Seahawks had to also get Jalen Milroe, who has not appeared in a regular-season game since Week 5 of last year, ready to play in case they needed to turn to their third quarterback against Arizona. He said Friday that they've had to manage Lock's reps this week, which was "more precautionary than anything else."

After Darnold suffered a glute injury on the fifth play of the opener, Lock played most of the first two games, posting an 82.5 Total QBR that ranked sixth best in that span. Three of his four touchdown passes came in a win 31-7 win over the Cardinals in Week 2.

The Seahawks also added some quarterback insurance earlier this week by signing former United Football League MVP Adrian Martinez to their practice squad.

Cross, Shaheed and Nwosu all missed the Bears game, while Williams went down in the third quarter. The only one of the four who practiced at all this week was Nwosu, who was limited Wednesday.

Josh Jones will start again at left tackle for Cross.

"The good news is, man, we've got a pretty steady room — that is improving — of defensive backs. ... I just feel like these guys are starting to play pretty good football for us. ... I like where we're at," Campbell said Friday, Nov. 6. "Depth wise, it's a pretty strong room. I don't like the thought of not having Reed, but at the same time, I'm encouraged. I think we'll be OK here."

As for what the Lions will do at the defensive end spot opposite of Aidan Hutchinson, Derrick Moore and Eric O'Neill stand out as options for increased roles. Campbell also mentioned undrafted rookie Anthony Lucas, who is currently on the practice squad.

"I mentioned this before, Brad (Holmes)'s done a good job with the depth that we've got," Campbell said. "We'll be able to weather the storm, and those guys are gonna get an opportunity. Adversity hits with injuries, that's the tough part. But the encouraging part is now guys get new opportunities, there's new guys now. You get your chance. What are you gonna do with it? That's encouraging because that's gonna help us grow."

Mays will be replaced in the starting lineup by Juice Scruggs.

Dan Campbell had a small update on linebacker Jack Campbell, who was carted off the field Nov. 1. Asked how the team is doing mentally, given the linebacker's injury, Dan Campbell said, "I think every day we've gotten better. We're getting a better handle on this, Jack continues to improve, which is all great news.

"This is about, man, how would he prepare, how would he play? Those are the standards for us going into this game. We owe it to him."

Jack Campbell was transported to Henry Ford Hospital after he got hurt against the Vikings. He put out a statement through the team Wednesday, saying he has "full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body."

ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals and Seattle Seahawks are ruling a total of ten players out for Sunday's Week 9 battle at Lumen Field.

The Cardinals are going to be without Jon Gaines II (ankle), Bam Knight (concussion) and Jayden Williams (knee) for their road test in Seattle.

Questionable for Arizona is Isaiah Adams (ankle), Max Melton (knee) and Walter Nolen III (ankle).

The Seahawks have a much lengthier list of players out this week:

Charles Cross (ankle), Sam Darnold (quad/ribs), Brandon Pili (back), Rashid Shaheed (knee), Leonard Williams (stinger), Quenton Nelson (knee), Uchenna Nwosu (ankle)

Connor O'Toole (foot) is questionable for Seattle.

What's Next for Cardinals-Seahawks?

The two teams can make up to two standard practice squad elevations this weekend, and with the amount of injuries on both sides, it wouldn't at all be surprising to see the Cardinals and Seahawks utilize both spots.

Pay special attention to who gets elevated, as this could be telling on who each team believes will be healthy (Cross in Seattle, Nolen in Arizona) entering Sunday.

The NFL mandates teams reveal final inactives 90 minutes before game time. For Sunday's 2:25 pm MST kickoff, that would be 12:55 pm.

Cardinals, Seahawks Prepare With New QBs

After trading Jacoby Brissett, the Cardinals are rolling with Gardner Minshew as their new starting quarterback — who spoke with reporters about the difficulty of staying focused on his role.

“Yeah naturally. I think over time that’s one of the things (I've) learned to handle better. I think everybody at this stage was the best wherever they came from," he said this week.

"I was used to that growing up and it is a different circumstance and everybody wants to be the guy out there, but you only have so much control over that. Focusing on the things that you can’t control is always a challenge and I feel like I’m proud of the way I did that this year.”

Drew Lock, meanwhile, will get the start for Darnold this week. Lock was under center against the Cardinals in Week 2, which was a blowout win for Seattle.

"You can see the stuff he liked and what they had success with," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said of prepping for Lock.

"Obviously, a lot has changed since Week 2. The first week is what it is. Week 2, you’re still kind of trying to find yourself and you’re not really even settled in yet as a team by any means. But yes, we can use that as a benefit for sure.”

title: Jack Campbell 'continues to improve,' Lions down starters vs Dolphins - Detroit Free Press

"Jack continues to improve, which is all great news and there again, this is about how would he prepare, how would he play," Dan Campbell said.
Branch was a full participant in practice Thursday, and Dan Campbell said he'll be re-evaluated after practice Friday but "I think BB’s going to be good here."

text:
Brian Branch is trending toward clearing concussion protocol in time to play in Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins, but the Detroit Lions likely will be without four other key starters.

Cornerback D.J. Reed (hip), defensive end D.J. Wonnum (concussion) and center Cade Mays (ankle) are not expected to play in NFL Week 9. Linebacker Jack Campbell remains hospitalized with a neck injury but is improving, Lions coach Dan Campbell said Friday in Allen Park.

"Jack continues to improve, which is all great news and there again, this is about how would he prepare, how would he play," Dan Campbell said. "Those are the standards for us going into this game, we owe it to him."

Branch was a full participant in practice Thursday, and Dan Campbell said he'll be re-evaluated after practice Friday but "I think BB’s going to be good here."

Reed, Wonnum and Mays did not practice Thursday because of injuries they suffered in last week's win over the Minnesota Vikings.

Reed injured his hip breaking up a fourth-and-5 pass one play after Jack Campbell's injury. Mays sprained his ankle in the first half. And Wonnum was hurt in a head-to-head collision initiated by Branch.

Safeties coach Jim O'Neil reiterated the team has no plans to rein in Branch's play on the field. Branch was fined for use of his helmet and an unnecessary roughness penalty in his return from a torn Achilles tendon in Week 7, and knocked himself and Wonnum out of last week's game.

"We coach eyes up, tackle, but we also coach we’re going to play the game and violently," O'Neil said. "That’s how the game was meant to be played. That’s one of the reasons BB is who he is. He’s got an old-school mentality, he’s explosive, he’s going to play the game violently. We talk about defending every blade of grass, whether it’s on the sideline – you’re not going to tip-toe the sideline on us. If a running back’s on his way down we’re going to beat him to the ground and hit him. I thought BB did a great job on that play."

At defensive end, rookie second-round pick Derrick Moore (Michigan) is expected to take most of Wonnum's snaps in pass rush packages, with undrafted rookies Eric O'Neill and Anthony Lucas also contributing.

And Dan Campbell said he likes the depth the Lions have in the cornerback room to help cover for the loss of Reed.

"Depth-wise, we’re a pretty strong room," Campbell said. "I don’t like the thought of not having Reed, but at the same time I’m encouraged. I’m encouraged. I think we’ll be OK here."

Malik Washington (31 catches, 329 yards) is the Dolphins' leading receiver.

text:
The Patriots are preparing to host the Green Bay Packers in a massive football weekend in Foxborough, culminating in Sunday's inter-conference showdown at Gillette Stadium.

On Friday, the Patriots ruled out WR A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) and RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness) for Week 9. New England is also listing seven players as questionable for Sunday's game: TE Hunter Henry (foot), S Kevin Byard III (chest), CB Carlton Davis III (neck), WR Mack Hollins (calf), OT Morgan Moses (foot), ST Brenden Schooler (hamstring), and OL Greg Van Roten (hamstring).

Hollins and Van Roten, who both opened their 21-day practice windows this week, are eligible to return from injured reserve. The team has until 4 p.m. ET on Saturday to activate the two veterans for them to be eligible to play on Sunday. New England has now used four of their eight IR-return designations, with Hollins and Van Roten joining WR A.J. Brown and OT Marcus Bryant as returnees. WR Romeo Doubs, starting LG Alijah Vera-Tucker, and FB Reggie Gilliam are among those who could also return this season.

Along with managing injured reserve, the Patriots continue to manage injuries to QB Drake Maye's supporting cast. After a knee "flare-up" in practice last week, Brown will miss his second straight game. Brown has played in only three games this season because of ankle and knee injuries, which is disappointing given the hype around the trade and how excited he was to play for his favorite childhood team.

The star wideout has just nine catches for 101 receiving yards while appearing in 3-of-8 games this season. Brown already missed four games with a stint on injured reserve and is now missing more time due to his knee injury. That's not ideal for the Patriots offense, and neither is the potential absence of one of Maye's most reliable targets, TE Hunter Henry. Henry was injured in the second quarter after playing only eight plays vs. the Dolphins last week when he went down to make a catch breaking into the sideline.

After sitting out the first two practices this week, Henry returned in a limited capacity on Friday, a positive sign that he could give it a go Sunday. Henry leads the Pats with 29 catches and ranks second on the team with 326 receiving yards, which is 12th among tight ends this season. The Patriots captain has produced +28.6 total expected points on his 29 receptions, ranking ninth among tight ends. Maye has never played a full game in his three-year career without Henry.

That said, the hope is that Hollins's return will boost the Patriots offense on Sunday. In the first four weeks of the season, Hollins led the team in receptions (15) and receiving yards (209) as one of Maye's go-to targets. The veteran wideout has a well-rounded skill set as a blocker, a dirty-area receiver over the middle, and a large catch radius that seems to give Maye comfort when he targets Hollins downfield (6-4, 221).

If the Patriots activate Hollins, their available wide receivers would be DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, Efton Chism III, and Hollins. At tight end, New England will likely lean on rookie Eli Raridon, while hoping Henry is available alongside blockers Cameron Latu and Tanner Arkin. Last week, lead back Rhamondre Stevenson played 45 snaps (76.3%), with spell-back Corey Kiner (11 snaps, two explosive runs) and RB Lan Larison (five snaps) behind Stevenson. On the offensive line, the expectation is the Patriots will roll with the group they ended the game with in Miami: LT Will Campbell, LG Ben Brown, C Jared Wilson, RG Matt Pryor, and RT Morgan Moses.

With the Packers coming in as the seventh-ranked defense in expected points added (EPA), it'll be a tough matchup for the shorthanded Patriots offense. Ideally, New England's mostly healthy defense could pick up some of the slack so there's less pressure on the offense to win a shootout. On Thursday, top nickel cornerback Marcus Jones was a non-participant with a foot injury. However, Jones returned to Friday's practice and won't carry an injury designation into the game – he's good to go.

The other injuries on the Patriots defense we've been monitoring are to edge rushers Dre'Mont Jones (knee/shoulder) and rookie Gabe Jacas (knee). Jacas has been terrific in his first season, leading all rookie EDGEs in run stops (10) and is second in quarterback pressures (23) behind only No. 3 overall pick David Bailey (26). However, the second-rounder didn't finish last week's game vs. the Dolphins after injuring his knee in the third quarter, while Jones has been playing through bumps and bruises all year. Like Jones, Jacas and Dre'Mont Jones are off the injury report and are good to go.

Lastly, as expected, Packers star edge rusher Micah Parsons (knee) won't play this week after opening his 21-day practice window to return from injured reserve. Parsons is working his way back from tearing his ACL and meniscus last December in a game vs. the Broncos. The goal is for Parsons to return in the coming weeks, but the star pass-rusher won't be ready to play the Patriots on Sunday. Green Bay will also be down starting C Sean Rhyan (ankle) on their interior offensive line.

Although most of the attention will be on Rob Gronkowski's Patriots Hall of Fame induction ceremony, New England will need to manage its roster on Saturday. As mentioned, the Patriots have until 4 p.m. ET on Saturday to activate Hollins and Van Roten from injured reserve. The Pats have one open roster spot, so they'd need to create another opening on the 53-man roster to make room for both veterans. The Patriots could also elevate players from the practice squad by Saturday's roster deadline – we'll keep you updated.

With several legends in attendance, including team Hall of Famers in Gronkowski and Tom Brady, the Patriots will host the Packers at 4:25 p.m. ET at Gillette Stadium on Sunday.
